threads.answer:
Dear
Thank you for your inquiry and for your patience. We have consulted with several partners in order to provide you with appropriate responses to your questions. Please see below.
Question 1: We represent applicants with work permit requests submitted before COVID started in middle March. Some ofthese clients have already completed biometrics, but final decisions have not been made. These workers would contribute to essential services according to the provincial definition of Ontario and some according to the Federal Definition. Can we request IRCC to finalize these work permit applications, i.e. request exemption from the travel restrictions?
COVID-19 program delivery instructions have been issued for new and existing temporary residence, permanent residence and citizenship applications in Canada and abroad.
Applications will not be refused for non-compliance, and all applications currently in progress at IRCC offices abroad and at case processing centres will continue to be processed but may experience delays.
Temporary workers: Prioritizing work permit processing for critical occupations
Applicants outside Canada can continue to submit work permit applications; however, due to the impacts of COVID- 19, IRCC is operating at reduced capacity and may not be able to process applications normally or provide accurate processing times.
IRCC is currently prioritizing work permit processing for critical occupations in select National Occupational Classification (NOC) codes related to agricultural, agri-food, truck driving and health, as these occupations have been
identified as critical for Canada. Consult the full list of critical occupations for priority processing.
Non-prioritized applications will be processed as operational capacity allows where all processing requirements are
met.
Question 2: If a worker's position can be classified as part of an essential service, must the provincial or federal definition be used to determine whether a person is eligible for exemption from travel restrictions?
In response to the COVID-19 outbreak, the federal Government of Canada has issued a series of Orders in Council, including establishing which foreign nationals are permitted entry to Canada. These Orders in Council have a direct impact on foreign workers, as follows:
Foreign nationals who are currently outside Canada are not subject to Canada's travel restrictions if they are travelling to Canada for a non-optional or non-discretionary purpose and they meet the following conditions:
1. The foreign national holds a valid Canadian work permit as defined in section R2; or
2. The foreign national received a positive decision from lRCC on a work permit application but whose work permit has not yet beenissued.
Cioyenneté Canada Examples of non-optional or non-discretionary travel for temporary workers may include:
A foreign national has a letter of introduction for an employer-specific work permit, holds a valid job offer and will be able to work once they enter Canada.
A foreign national has a letter of introduction for an open work permit, holds a valid job offer and will be able to work once they enter Canada.
A foreign national has a valid work permit and ordinarily resides in Canada. Whether the foreign national's employment still exists or if they are currently laid off is not determinative in this case. What is determinative is that the foreign national's primary residence is in Canada (suggesting their travel is not optional).
For more information, consult Determining whether entry of temporary workers will be for a discretionary or optional purpose
Question 3: Can applications that were submitted for essential services in May and June 2020 (after COVID rules where implemented) be finalized if biometrics are not required (agriculture workers)?
Due to the ongoing service disruptions related to COVID-19, IRCC has put in place a public policy to temporarily exempt foreign workers in certain sectors, namely the agriculture, agri-food and health-care sectors, from having to give their biometrics before coming to Canada if biometric collection services are unavailable to them.
For applicants who are not covered under the public policy, if the visa application centres (VACs) or other biometrics collection sites in your country or region are still closed, and your extension to give biometrics is ending, you will not have to give biometrics until the biometrics collection sites reopen. This applies to you, even if your biometrics instruction letter (BIL) says you have 30 or 90 days. Your application will not be refused or closed if you cannot give your biometrics due to COVID-19 service disruptions.
Question 4: If an agriculture worker have been exempted from biometrics and the work permit issued, will the spouse that requested also be issued with a work permit without biometrics, or will the work permit decision for both be held back until biometrics can be completed.
The temporary public policy exempting essential workers from giving biometrics overseas applies only to workers whose National Occupation Classification (NOC) code falls under one of the following:
agricultural and agri-food sectors
●health-care sector
truck drivers
Therefore, the public policy would not apply to an accompanying spouse's open work permit application.
For applicants who are not covered under the public policy, if the visa application centres (VACs) or other biometrics collection sites in your country or region are still closed, and your extension to give biometrics is ending, you will not have to give biometrics until the biometrics collection sites reopen. This applies to you, even if your biometrics instruction letter (BIL) says you have 30 or 90 days. Your application will not be refused or closed if you cannot give your biometrics due to COVID-19 service disruptions.

IRCC.COVID-TravelExemptions-Exemptionsdevoyage-COVID.IRCC@cic.gc.ca 5 weeks ago. See enclosed.

threads.subject: Approved for Sending: Submitting a work permit extension / receiving date is next day / out of status? --REP- 2020-1253
threads.question:
Hello,
Question:
Submitting a work permit extension on the day it expires and it is not received by IRCC until the next day due to time zones, are they out of status?
Response:
A temporary resident must apply to extend their period of authorized stay before it ends. For online applications, our system uses Universal Time Standard (UTC) around the world to ensure that time is equal for all. Therefore, we do not go based on ‘time zones’ but that an application must be submitted before midnight UTC on the day the status expires.
The date received for paper applications is the date physically received and stamped at the Case Processing Centre. If the date physically received is after the expiry date of the applicants status, they will count back 7 days and use that date as the date received’.
If our system shows that the application was received after midnight on the day of expiry, the applicant does not benefit from the automatic extension of their status under R183(5), nor do they meet the requirements of R186(u) to benefit from the authorization to work without a permit.
Applicants who have lost their temporary resident status and authorization to work can apply for restoration of status within 90 days of their permit expiry date. When applying for restoration of status, applicants must provide a detailed account ofhow/why they came to be out of status. Applications for restoration of status are assessed on a case by case basis.
The and Citizenship Help Centre offers many useful resources. You may find the following page helpful: How can I check if my application has been received? Also, more information on work permit extensions and restoration of status applications (including full eligibility details) can be found here: Guide 5553: Applying for a work permit inside Canada-extend. change conditions, initial and open work permits.
Thank you kindly,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.question:
Hello
Thank you for your inquiry.
We apologize for the misunderstanding regarding the restoration of status for the purposes of a PGWP.
There has been a recent update to the Program Delivery Instructions (PDI) regarding the PGWP and restoration of status.
If an applicant's study permit expires before they apply for the PGWP, they must restore their status as a student and apply for the PGWP within 90 days of the study permit expiry or they must leave Canada and apply for the PGWP overseas.
Based on the new PDI updates, the applicants can now apply online directly for the PGWP, pay the correct fee ($255) and also pay the fee to restore their status as a student ($350) in the same application. Due to system limitations, applicants must pay the fees to restore their status as a student online and attach a copy of the receipt to their PGWP online application. Applicants do not need to make a separate application to restore their status as a student.

Good day,
Thank you for your request and our apologies for the delay.
Question:
If my client's IEC POE letter expires during the banned entry to Canada for foreigners, can I submit a request for extension of validity of POE letter through webform? Please kindly advise.
Response:
Foreign nationals who are participating in the International Experience Canada (IEC) program receive a letter of introduction that is valid for one year after its date of issue. If their letter expires within the next 30 days, and they cannot travel due to disruptions caused by COVID-19, IEC applicants can contact IRCC for a 90-day extension using this web form. On this web form, applicants should select “International Experience Canada” from the drop-down menu and include as many details as possible to support their case.
If they have already received a 90-day extension to their current letter of introduction, applicants can request a second extension of an additional 90 days. Please see COVID-19: International Experience Canada applicants for more information.
All applications for extensions should be made 30 days before the expiry date. If the holder's letter expires in 60 days or more, they should wait until a month before the expiry to contact IRCC. Please note, if they do not receive a confirmation email from IRCC, it does not mean their application was not received. Applicants should continue checking their IRCC account for updates.
Thank you kindly,

threads.subject: Approved for Sending: Temporary lay-off and use of same work permit upon return to work -- REP-2020-0785
threads.question:
Hello,
Question:
Temporary foreign worker receives a temporary lay-off (per provincial standards) for a period of 3 months due to declining business resulting from the COVID-19 crisis. The TF W is on a LMIA-based work permit (NOC A, high skilled and high wage). Can the TFW use their existing work permit to return to work? Or must the employer obtain a new LMIA and then the employee must obtain a new work permit?
Same scenario as above except the TF W is on a LMIA-exempt work permit (eg. NAFTA).
Response:
The temporary foreign worker may return to work with their existing permit if the following conditions are met:
he work permit is still valid.
here are have been no changes in the employment conditions (including location, occupation, or employer).
he LMIA held by the employer remains valid as determined by its “Assessment Expiry Date" (indicated on the hard copy); OR the employer is permitted to hire in an LMIA-exempt situation using the employer portal.
Under R185(b) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations, a foreign worker will require a new work permit if there has been a change in employer, occupation, or location. However, due to COVID-19, a public policy has been implemented to facilitate this process. This public policy enables temporary workers in Canada with authorization to work (that is, a valid work permit or authorization to work without a permit) who are required to obtain a new employer-specific work permit before commencing a new job to begin working while their work permit application is pending. More information on this public policy can be found on the following page: Public policy on exemptions to work permit conditions when changing employment: COVID-19 program delivery.
If the employer’s LMIA is no longer valid, they must follow the procedure to obtain a new one before the temporary foreign worker is authorized to return to work. More information about obtaining an LMIA can be found on the following page: Find out ifyou need a Labour Market Impact Assessment.
Lastly, employers are encouraged to complete an Employer Compliance Voluntary Disclosure form to notify IRCC of any changes to employment conditions, including layoffs as a result of COVID-19. It is advisable to submit these forms as promptly as possible following any changes in order for IRCC to maintain up-to-date employer files and to help ensure that employers remain compliant. More information on voluntary disclosure can be found on the following page: IMP: Voluntary Disclosure for Employers.
Thank you kindly,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

requirements -- REP-2020-1126
Good Day,

Question:
We understand that a candidate has to have at least one year of skilled work experience inside Canada within the 3 years prior to application in order to meet minimum eligibility criteria for the Canadian Experience Class ("MEC"). We understand skilled work experience in Canada within the 10 years prior to application can be awarded Express Entry Comprehensive
Ranking System points ("CRS").
Is there any other difference in assessing skilled work experience in Canada for the purposes of meeting MEC versus CRS?
Must each year of skilled work experience in Canada equal 365 days of foot-on-ground work experience in Canada for the

Answer:
Canadian Work Experience for the purposes of CEC MEC and CRS points are assessed the same.
The intent of the Canadian Experience Class (CEC) is to make permanent residence more accessible to skilled workers who have demonstrated an ability to integrate into the Canadian labour market. The CEC is for workers who can economically integrate in Canada, which is demonstrated in part by the accumulation of 1,560 hours of skilled Canadian work experience in the three years preceding their application for permanent residence. This experience must be acquired while in Canada.
Each case is assessed based on its own merit, and IRCC recognizes that some occupations require periods of business travel outside Canada. However, the policy intent of the program is to offer a pathway to permanent residence for those who have integrated in the Canadian workforce. The decision to approve or refuse is at the discretion of the officer reviewing the case and it will be based on the information available to them at the time of the decision.

threads.question:
Ce:
Hello
This is a great question to be asked, and we would like to clarify the understanding of "biometrics are not presently required given the Covid-19 situation".
Depending on the line of business (LOB), there is a Public Policy (Pub Pol) exempting temporary foreign service workers from providing their biometrics. The Pub Pol is not extended to other Temporary Residency (TR) applications (such as Study or Visitors) and also excludes Permanent Residency (PR) applications.
Even if applicants are not yet authorized to travel to Canada, when biometrics collection sites re-open, they must provide their biometrics. In order to provide their biometrics, client's will need to pay the biometric fee (individual rate of CAN $85, Family rate of CAN $170, or Group rate (i.e. performing artist) of $255) to receive a Biometric Instruction Letter (BIL) to submit their photograph and fingerprints.
Given that Service Canada offices are closed, client's eligible for the Pub Pol (of workers within Canada changing jobs or employers) may not need to give their biometrics when they apply for a new work permit. After an applicant applies, and their fees are paid, IRCC will verify if the exemption applies to them. Should they meet the Pub Pol criteria, IRCC will issue a refund for their biometrics fee.
Lastly, applicant's should always verify if they have valid biometrics on file. Those who have applied for TR would have biometrics that are valid for 10 years, and that can be used for another visitor visa, study permit or work permit application.
For information on overseas temporary foreign workers (TFWs) please see web page: Temporary public policy exempting essential workers from giving biometrics overseas: [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/news/notices/public-policy-biometrics-exemption.html](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/news/notices/public-policy-biometrics-exemption.html)

threads.subject: Home Child Care Provider Pilot -- REP-2020-1363
threads.question:
Dear Sir or Madam,
I am a lawyer member ofLaw Society of Alberta and my membership number is I have a client who requested some clarification regarding the above-mentioned program and I was not able to find it in the published instruction. She would like to know whether she is able to have different employers and working full time in total. Also, whether it is mandatory for the employer to have a business number and open the payroll account or it is enough to have an agreement and payment arrangement in between.
I appreciate it if you could advise me.
Thank you,
Kind regards,
threads.answer:
Immigration Representatives / Représentants inmigration (IRCC)
Dear
Thank you for contacting the Immigration Representative Mailbox.
Yes, the Home Child Care Providers (4411) and Home Support Worker (4412) full-time work can be accumulated through working for more than one employer at the same time. However, the applicant would need to demonstrate that they meet all requirements.
Note that the initial job offer for an applicant with less than 24 months experience must be for full-time employment' with one Canadian employer (one CRA business number). There may be two employers associated to the CRA business number (for instance, Mr. and Mrs. Smith, for that one full-time employment).
If an applicant is approved under that job offer, they would need to be mindful that their acceptance under the pilot was based on the information in that job offer (e.g., work description, details about the individuals requiring care, hours of work, wages, etc.). As such, an applicant approved under the pilot should carefully consider the risk in changing employers, particularly if the new work arrangement that differs substantially from the initial job offer. For example, accumulating part-time employment for multiple employers to make 30 hours of work in a week may or may not be considered by an officer to be equivalent to 30 hours of eligible full-time care, as the part-time do not appear consistent with the full-time care needs of the person receiving care.
The occupation-restricted open work permit is a program design feature that is provided, in place of an employer-specified work permit, in order to facilitate the change of employers when required (for instance, if an employer terminated employment, or does not meet obligations towards the employee, or is abusive). It was not intended to be used to seek alternative forms of employment in those occupations (for instance, in institutional caregiving situations, or placement-agency based part-time work, where care needs are generally different and travel time may be included in the hours of work). This is because the programs are in place to meet a specific labour market need (the full-time in-home caregiving needs of Canadian families).
Yes, under the Home Child Care Provider and Home Support Worker pilots, the employer is required to obtain a CRA business number. In Canada, legislation requires that an individual who hires and pays an employee must open a payroll program account. It should also be noted that the Ministerial Instructions do specify that prospective employers of applicants who have less than 24 months of experience must have a Canada Revenue Agency business number.
The CRA account is required because the employer has responsibilities in the employment relationship (e.g., requirement to calculate and withhold payroll deduetions and remit (pay) source deductions). Individuals hiring a caregiver or home support worker can easily obtain a business number and open a payroll program account. For more information, you may visit Canada Revenue Agency's webpages Employing a caregiver, baby-sitter, or domestic worker and Business number registration.
We trust that this information will be of assistance.
and Citizenshi Canada et Ciloyeneé Canada
Sincerely,
The Immigration Representative Mailbox

threads.subject: 'Health Services' Definition--(REP-2019-2143)-- REP-2020-1368 -- due July 23, 2020
threads.question:
Good day,
Thank you for your question to IRCC immigration representatives mailbox.
Question: I sent questions below regarding work as an optometric technician/receptionist without having a done a medical. Question 2 was answered by your team as follows:
1. In the event that someone works in that field on a study or work permit, without having done a medical exam, and later applies for another temporary or permanent resident application, what are the consequences?
Answer: The instructions currently in effect indicate that the person should repeat the medical examination to obtain an extension of their work permit in Canada in accordance with subparagraph 30(1)(a)(ii) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR). Your application may be refused if a medical exam is not done.
If this person had stopped working that job, they wouldn't need to get an new work permit because they are no longer in the medical field. Would this past period of work workout the medical done have to be declared on subsequent permanent resident or work permit applications?I had asked above what the consequences were, but did not receive a clear answer.
Response: The requirement for a medical examination is specified in paragraph A16(2)(b) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA). Subparagraph R30(1)(a)(ii) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR) makes it mandatory for those seeking work in an occupation in which the protection of public health is essential to complete a medical examination.
The above requirements apply to any foreign national working as an optical technician/receptionist, as this position is considered to be within the field of health services. As such, working in this occupation without completing a medical examination may be considered non-compliance with IRPA and could result in a report written under section A44 for violating section A41: Non-compliance with Act. Working in this occupation without a medical examination can be considered non-compliance regardless of whether the specific condition is imposed on the foreign national's work permit under section R185 of the IRPR. The consequence of such a written report would be the loss of status in Canada and possible removal of the foreign national.
If the foreign national wishes to submit subsequent IRCC applications, it is very likely they will have to disclose information about their employment history. It is an obligation for applicants to provide truthful and accurate information under subsection A16(1) of IRPA. The application for a work permit includes a section for applicants to report all positions of employment held in the 10 years prior to submission. If this section is not completed accurately, it could lead to a finding of misrepresentation under paragraph A40(1)(a) of IRPA and a subsequent five year bar to any entry to Canada.
Even if a finding of inadmissibility is not made, an officer may be prohibited from issuing a work permit as per R200(3)(e) of the IRPR which states that an officer shall not issue a work permit to a foreign national if the foreign national has engaged in unauthorized study or work in Canada or has failed to comply with a condition of a previous permit or authorization unless
"(ii) the study or work was unauthorized by reason only that the foreign national did not comply with conditions imposed
under paragraph 185(a), any of subparagraphs 185(b)(i) to (iii) or paragraph 185(c)."
If the condition to not work in a health services position was imposed on the work permit and an officer determines that the foreign national only failed to comply with this one condition (imposed under R185(b)(i)), they could still issue the work
permit. However, final decisions are made at the assessing officer's discretion.
The following pages may be helpful for more information: Conditions and validity period on work permits (temporary workers) Work permit issuance prohibitions
Sincerely,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

Similarly, an applicant can receive 50 points if they are working in a NOC O, A, or B position in Canada if working on a work permit issued based on a positive LMlA as long as other conditions are met.

Question: At the time of filing the PR application, the applicants meet the requirements, namely: Each applicant holds 10% or more of the voting rights attached to all shares of the corporation outstanding at that time; and Applicants and the designated entity jointly hold more than 50% of the total voting rights attached to all shares of the corporation outstanding at that time. threads.subject: CLOSED: Residency exemption for Minor applying for citizenship -- REP-2020-1566 --
threads.question:
Hello
A child is eligible to apply for a Grant of Canadian Citizenship under section 5(2) of the Citizenship Act if they meet the following requirements (available here): To be eligible for a grant of Canadian citizenship, the minor must:
- be under 18 years of age at the time the application is signed;
- be a permanent resident of Canada;
- have at least one parent (includes legally adoptive parent) who is a Canadian citizen or who will become a citizen at the same time as the minor (applying together as a family).
Note: A step parent or grandparent is not considered a parent for citizenship application purposes unless that step parent or
grandparent has legally adopted the minor.
Minor children must not:
- be subject to any prohibition under the Citizenship Act (see section 11 of the application form CIT 0003); and/or
- have any unfulfilled conditions relating to their permanent resident status; and/or
- be under a removal order (asked by Canadian officials to leave Canada)
Note: A guardian may file an application on behalf of a minor child as long as the minor has at least one parent who is a
Canadian citizen.
Question #9B must be completed on the application form according to the following instructions (from the Application guide):
You must let us know if the minor left Canada for a total of 730 days or more in the past five (5) years or since becoming a permanent resident.
If yes, give details of the time the minor spent away from Canada. Use another piece of paper, if you need more space.
If the child meets the above conditions for a Grant of Citizenship, they are eligible so long as they continue to retain their permanent resident status (they must be valid permanent residents as of the day Citizenship would be granted). If the child has not met the requirements to maintain their PR status in Canada, or they may lose their PR status before a decision is made on their Citizenship application, it will affect their eligibility for Canadian Citizenship.
Regards, The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

- neither parent is physically in Canada.

threads.answer:
Dear
Our apologies for the delay in our response.
A temporary public policy was issued on August 24, 2020, to allow certain temporary residents in Canada with valid visitor status to apply for an employer-specific work permit from within Canada, if they were in Canada on that date and remain in the country.
Under the caregiver Ministerial Instructions, the work permit refusal to process (RTP) only applies where all of the following conditions are met:
(a) the applicant is outside Canada;
(b) the applicant is making an initial work permit application (e.g. does not currently hold a valid work permit);
(c) the applicant intends to engage in work as described under National Occupation Classification (NOC) 4411 (excluding foster parents) and 4412 (excluding housekeepers);
(d) the applicant is destined to a job location outside Quebec; and
(e) the assessment, by Employment and Social Development Canada, and on the basis of which the officer must make a determination pursuant to paragraphs 203(1)(a) to (e) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations, was requested on or after June 18, 2019.
Therefore, for the duration that the public policy is in effect, visitors in Canada who meet all of the August 24 public policy eligibility requirements would not be subject to the work permit RTP for caregivers.

[https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-) manuals/service-delivery/coronavirus/travel-restrictions.html#family-reunification I am not sure if this situation is considered as a family unification or a dependent child can simply accompany his father who holds a valid WP. Also, “In order for a foreign national to be eligible under this exemption, there must be two or more foreign nationals who are immediate family members of each other, and authorizing one or more of them to enter Canada must allow them to be reunited." threads.answer:
Good day,
Thank you for your request and our apologies for the delay.
Question: Under the current situation, can WP holder (visa exempt) fly to Canada with a minor child?
FW's family unification allows only when FW resides in Canada.
[https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-) manuals/service-delivery/coronavirus/travel-restrictions.html#family-reunification
I am not sure if this situation is considered as a family unification or a dependent child can simply accompany his father who holds a valid WP.
Also, "In order for a foreign national to be eligible under this exemption, there must be two or more foreign nationals who are immediate family members of each other, and authorizing one or more of them to enter Canada must allow them to be reunited."
Does it mean that there must be a family unit already in Canada (thus the 2 or more immediate in Canada whether they are worker, visitor) in order to justify bringing others to re-unite with them. So if there was only one person, but the majority of the family unit is back in home country, then maybe no justification to bring them to Canada to reunite.
Response: IRCC has implemented exemptions to the current pandemic travel restrictions to facilitate the reunification of immediate family members. These exemptions (detailed here) currently allow foreign nationals whose travel to Canada is authorized in writing by an officer designated under subsection 6(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act to travel for the purpose of reuniting immediate family members. The above passage (from the same page) that you have quoted is meant to reiterate the necessity of reunification between at least two family members. The location of the majority of the family unit is not a factor in this exemption.
The family reunification guidelines also allow immediate family members to accompany a principal applicant (or work permit holder) while travelling to Canada. It should be noted that travel must still be considered non-optional and non-discretionary. Generally, those accompanying family members seeking to establish themselves in Canada are considered to be travelling for a non-discretionary purpose. More information on non-optional and non-discretionary travel can be found at the following page: Non-optional and non-discretionary travel: COVID-19 program delivery.
Accompanying family members must seek written authorization from IRCC prior to making travel arrangements. Valid written authorization is required in order to board an airplane to Canada. To request written authorization, foreign nationals are advised to contact IRCC at IRCC.COVID-TravelExemptions-Exemptionsdevoyage-COVID.IRCC@cic.gc.ca. This email is to be used for family reunification requests only. It is necessary to provide the following information:
- full name
- date of birth
- unique client identifier (UCI)
- passport number
- detailed reason for travel
- proof of relationship with an immediate family member in Canada
- proof of immigration status of your immediate family member in Canada (copy of their study permit or work permit)
- proof of temporary resident visa or eTA
More Information and details regarding the written authorization process is available on the following page: Coronavìrus disease (COVID-19) and visitors to Canada: Uniting with immediate family members.
Regards, The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

There is no set list of specific occupations to avoid for clients that have these conditions imposed on them for their open work permit. threads.question:
Good day,
Thank you for your question. Our sincere apologies for the delay in responding.
The answer to this question depends on the length of the program of study. If the duration of the program of study is longer than 6 months, the student must apply for a study permit to begin studying in Canada. This continues to apply even if courses have temporarily been shifted online due to COVID-19. This is because the courses may eventually return to an in-person instruction format, thus necessitating that the student hold a valid study permit to participate. If the program has permanently shifted online, the person is not eligible for a study permit and cannot apply for one. They can, however, participate in the program so long as they continue to hold valid status in Canada or choose to leave Canada.
For more information, please consult our Program Delivery Instructions.

The discretion of an officer is always dependent on the type of application and level of information provided.
Any requirement to factor in BlOC depends entirely on the type of application that has been submitted by the client. Operational Manuals and other online resources are interpretations of IRPA and IRPR that also assist officers during their decision-making process. Question:
Dear Sir/Madam -we have a client who sent a European employee to Canada as a business visitor to do after-sales service work. Answer:
NIELs are valid for single use only. Each time the person wants to travel to Canada, if they believe they need a national interest exemption, they should contact their nearest visa office as stated on the GoC website: [https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-) manuals/service-delivery/coronavirus/travel-restrictions.html#national
Note that the travel restrictions and exemptions have changed since July and some individuals who required NIELs before now do not, specifically if they are technicians performing installation, inspection, maintenance, or repair of equipment necessary to support critical infrastructure:
Section 3(1)(j)(i)of the Order in Council, Minimizing the Risk of Exposure to COVID-19 in Canada (Prohibition of Entry into Canada from any country other than the United States), provides an exemption to the travel restrictions for:
(j)a person or any person in a class of persons who, as determined by the Chief Public Health Officer (CPHO) appointed under subsection 6(1) of the Public Health Agency of Canada Act (ii)will provide an essential service while in Canada As of October 8, 2020, this determination by the CPHO now includes installation work in addition to inspection, maintenance and repair equipment necessary to support critical infrastructure. The updated CPHO determination for this group exemption is attached for your reference. Travellers do not require a letter from the Government of Canada in order to be exempt under 3(1)(j)(ii) of the Order and the onus is on the applicant to satisfy the airline and border officials that they are exempt from the travel restrictions. Documentary evidence must explicitly state they will be installing, inspecting, repairing or maintaining equipment required to support critical infrastructure. Border officials are responsible for the administration of Emergency Orders made under the Quarantine Act at Canada’s ports
et Ciloyenneé Canada
of entry. As such, the final determination on entry to Canada and subsequent public health measures will be determined by a border official who is required to weigh the evidence present at the time of entry against reasonableness and the overall risks to public health.

threads.answer:
Hello,
QUESTION: Under this temporary public policy, as an American, can he avail of this LMIA EXEMPT offer of employment (he is now a licensed Chiropractor in Alberta) under the International Mobility Program even if he is LIVING in Canada right now?
RESPoNSE: The public policy allowing visitors in Canada to apply for an employer-specific work permit is not an LMIA-exemption. It is simply a waiver of the normal requirement of section 199 if the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations on who may apply after entry. The beginning of the instructions on how to apply can be found here: If you're a visitor who needs a work permit
The eligibility is copied below for ease of reference:
Apply online under a public policy
Normally, visitors can't apply for work permits from inside Canada. Due to COVID-19, visitors can now apply online for an employer-specific work permit by following the steps below.
Who's eligible You must
- have been physically present in Canada on August 24, 2020 。if you left Canada and returned after August 24, you can't apply this way
- be a visitor with valid status when you apply for the work permit 。if your visitor status has expired, you'll need to restore your visitor status before you apply for a work permit
The public policy doesn't change the requirement for a Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) or LMIA-Exempt offer of employment. To obtain an LMIA-exempt, employer-specific work permit the visitor must still meet the requirements of the LMIA-exemption category they are applying under. Simply being in Canada does not meet any of the LMIA-exemption requirements.
You can find the information on whether an LMlA is required or not by reviewing this web page: Hire a temporary foreign worker. You can find more specific information on the LMIA-exemption process for employers on this public page: Hire a worker without an LMIA. If there is an employer whose
situation falls within one of the LMIA-exemption categories, then, yes, the employer must use the Employer Portal to submit the formal offer.
I note that you state: If it is through the IMP (the requirement is for the foreigner be outside of Canada when offering an employment via the employer portal) BUT the visitor is here in Canada. This statement is incorrect. There are very few specific LMIA-exemption categories that require the applicant to be outside of Canada. threads.answer:
Hello,
QuEsTioN: Will we need to apply to extend the extension for all cases nearing those set deadlines for which we won't have received a decision yet? Or will we have to tell our clients they have to depart at that time despite having an extension application pending?!
RESPoNSE: Although the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations authorizes the authority to work until a decision is made, the Department is using a 120 day period from the date of receipt of the application to provide a concrete date for employers and other service providers who have raised some challenges around "until a decision is made". Furthermore, the Departmental service standard for work permit renewal applications is 120 days and under normal circumstances is met over 90% of the time.
During the initial period of the pandemic, the processing time increased to beyond six months, in large part due to unavailability of biometric collection in Canada. However, the Department is aiming to bring processing times within service standards before February 2021 (i.e. 120 days following the October launch date). If an application extends beyond the 120 day expiry date in the letter, the applicant can contact the Department using the Web form to request a subsequent document or flag their case.
The letter does indicate that the authority to work is as per subsection 186(u) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations(IRPR) which would allow a person to continue working without a permit until a decision regardless of the end date on this letter. The letter does not overcome the IRPR, it is simply a facilitation document for applicants.

threads.subject: Question concernant les enfants de travailleurs étrangers temporaires dans le contexte de la COVID-19 -- REP- 2020-1053
threads.question:
Bonjour,
Selon les règlements d’IRCC, un enfant mineur qui désire étudier au Canada doit obtenir un permit d’études avant son arriver au Canada. Les conditions qui permet autrement ne s’applique que quand l’enfant se trouve déjà au Canada. Veuillez voir l'information ci-dessous :
« La dispense du permis d’études pour les mineurs en vertu du paragraphe 30(2) de la Loi sur l’immigration et la protection des réfugiés s’applique quand l’enfant mineur est déjà au Canada.
Par conséquent, les bureaux des visas qui traitent les demandes de résidence temporaire présentées à l’étranger par des enfants mineurs qui veulent étudier au Canada doivent les considérer comme des étudiants et non comme des visiteurs, même s’ils accompagnent un parent qui est autorisé à travailler ou à étudier au Canada. En d’autres mots, les enfants mineurs doivent être titulaires d’un permis d’études, à moins d’être dispensés de l’obligation d’en obtenir un au titre de l’article R188. »
Dans le cas de vos clients, l’enfant n’est pas au Canada est donc devrait appliquer pour un permis d’études avant de pouvoir étudier au Canada.
Cordialement,
Représentants immigration (IRCC)

threads.subject: Clarification on Study Permit Processing & Post-Graduate Work Permit Eligibility -- REP-2020-1553
threads.question:
Dear Imm Reps,
I am writing for clarification on Minister Mendicino's recently announced changes to facilitate online learning for international students. My questions regarding the announcement are outlined in red below.
The announcement indicates the new measures include:
- Providing priority study-permit processing for students who have submitted a complete application online, to ensure that permits are processed as quickly as possible. Does the priority study-permit processing apply to applicants who applied to restore their status inside Canada as a student (assuming the restoration/study permit application is deemed as complete)?
- Allowing students to count the time spent pursuing their studies online abroad toward their eligibility for a
Lnfomndduion post-graduation work permit, if they have submitted a study permit application and if at least 50% of their
program is completed in Canada. Does this also apply to applicants who have submitted
applications to restore their status inside Canada as a student? For example: An applicant has submitted a restoration of status (requesting their status be restored to that of a student) application, they are pursuing their studies online in Sept 2020, and will complete at least 50% of
their program in Canada. Will their time spent studying online, while the restoration/study permit
application is in process, count toward their post-graduate work permit eligibility, or does the study permit application need to be an "outside Canada" application? Thank you very much in advance for your attention to this! Please do not hesitate to let me know if you require any further information.
Yours truly,
threads.answer:
Good Day
We apologize for the delayed response. Here are the responses to your questions in the below email:
Foreign nationals applying for a restoration of status have lost their status and may not continue to work or attend school (in Canada or online) until their status has been restored and a new study permit has been issued. The priority processing is in regards to study permit applications submitted outside of Canada, it does not apply to in Canada study permit applications. For more information, please consult the following link Extend your Study Permit.
A study permit is required for programs inside Canada which are normally offered in-person but have moved to an online format due to COVID-19, unless they are shorter than 6 months in duration and therefore exempt from requiring a study permit under R188. A foreign national may therefore not begin studying such a program inside Canada or on an online format due to COVID-19 without a valid study permit, even if they have already submitted an application. If you do not have a valid study permit, you are not authorized to study, therefore no time studied without a valid study permit would count toward the PGWP.
Regards,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.subject: Student Permit Related Questions--REP-2020-1662
threads.question:
From Hello, I have a client how completed her 3 yr bachelors study program and now wants to continue
to study in a one year Masters program and to work at the same time. Her study permit expires in 2022, after the end of the planned ending of the Masters program. So she doesn't need a new study permit.
1. She qualifies for a post-graduation work permit (PGWP). If she gets the PGWP, is she permitted to both study full time in the Masters program and to work off campus in a non-
L'information divulguée en vertu de la loi sur laccés à Tinformaticr study related job for more than 20 hrs/wk simultaneously on the PGWP?
2. Her Master's program includes a co-op element. If she gets the PGWP, does she need a co-op work permit? Or would the PGWP alleviate the need for the Co-op work permit?
threads.answer:
Good day,
This is in response to your inquiry regarding eligibility of students who hold a post-graduation work permit to study and work full-time. If a foreign national holds both a study permit and a post-graduation work permit, they can study and work full-time as per the conditions of each permit. Please note that a study permit holder that also holds a PGWP, must continue to meet the conditions of R220.1 (1), which are to remain enrolled at a designated learning institution and actively pursue their studies.
In addition, as per paragraph R186(w), graduates who apply for a work permit, such as a post-graduation work permit, before the expiry of their study permit are eligible to work full time without a work permit while waiting for a decision on their application if all of the following apply:
- They are or were the holders of a valid study permit at the time of the post-graduation work permit application. They have completed their program of study.
- They met the requirements for working off campus without a work permit under paragraph R186(v) (that is, they were a full-time student enrolled at a DLl in a post-secondary academic, vocational or professional training program of at least 8 months in duration that led to a degree, diploma or certificate). They did not exceed the allowable hours of work under paragraph R186(v).
The PGWP provide the client with the authorization to work full-time in Canada. Therefore, if a client holds a valid post-graduation work permit, there is no need for them to apply for a co-op work permit. Thank you and have a nice day,

Can one apply for Express Entry (e-APR) if he has an implied status (Extension of visitor, student, or worker status)?
Response: Yes. However, the type of permit the applicant is on at the time of application for permanent residence may affect the FSW and CRS points for arranged employment. For more information, please consult our webpage.
- Can one apply for Bridging Open Work Permit application considering the below situations? Implied Status for Worker: Can one apply for Bridging Open Work Permit, if he had applied to extend his PGWP (despite not being eligible) before it expires to buy some time, has an implied status and the decision is not yet made, his EE PR application is in process, and now wishes to apply for BOWP based on this situation?
Response: No, as the applicant must have a valid work permit that expires in 4 months or less to qualify for a BOwP (and meet all other requirements -See below).
Implied Status for Visitor: Can one apply for Bridging Open Work Permit while his Express Entry application is in process and he has applied for change of status from Worker to Visitor so that he can stay in Canada legally while his PR application gets finalized, and the decision is not yet made on this application? Meaning he applied for Visitor Record before his Work Permit expires, has an implied status and the decision is not yet made, and now wishes to apply for BOwP so that he can resume/continue working while his PR application is in process. In this case, would he fall under the "worker implied status" or "visitor implied status" due to change in status application, and if this situation benefits him for applying BOWP?
Response: No, to be eligible for a BOWP, foreign nationals must:
be currently in Canada
- have valid status on a work permit that is due to expire within the next 4 months be the principal applicant on an APR under the FSWC, the CEC, the FSTC, the PNC (see note below), the AFP or 1 of the 2 caregiver classes (submitted before June 18, 2019) have completed one of the following APR stages: o electronic application for permanent residence (e-APR) submitted under Express Entry has passed the section 10 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR) completeness check; or o receipt of a positive eligibility assessment on their paper APR submitted by mail under one of the economic classes above have applied for an open work permit
Cioyenneté Canada
- have paid the work permit processing fee and the open work permit holder fee
- have provided, as applicable, evidence that their provincial nomination is unrestricted (for example, nomination certificate)
Note: Foreign nationals in the Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) are eligible for a BOwP only if they have provided a copy of
the nomination letter issued by the nominating province or territory along with their application, and there is no indication that employment restrictions exist as conditions of the nomination.
For more information, please consult our website.
- Can we apply for PGWP and TRV from inside Canada in the same application? Or, apply PGWP first and once it is obtained, apply for TRV? When applying for TRV from inside Canada, what would we really write in From and To dates to request TRV? Is it same as PGWP From and To dates? Do we get the TRV for 10 years by default or as per PGWP only?
Response: Students in Canada who wish to extend or change their temporary resident status cannot submit an application for a Temporary Resident Visa (TRV) in the same application as the PGWP because a valid work or study permit is required for the issuance of a TRV from inside Canada. In addition, a new TRV will not be issued at the time of the PGWP approval; therefore, applicants will need to apply for a new visitor visa separately after the PGWP application is approved. The TRV would be issued for 10 years, or up to the expiry of the passport, whichever expires first. Please note, foreign nationals applying from inside Canada must submit their application by electronic means only, unless otherwise specified.
Can we apply for second application if one is already in process? -- For e.g. A student in Canada is waiting for his PGWP or has his PGWP but does have a job in NOC O, A or B with 3 paystubs as of yet. His wife applied for visitor record (change of status from open work permit to visitor record) and the application is in process. But once the student obtains his PGWP and/or job in NOC O, A or B with 3 paystubs, can we apply for SOWP for his wife again while the visitor record application is still in process? If yes, what should be the best way? Because if we withdraw the visitor record application first, then the applicant will have no status, and with the new SOwP application we would also have to restore the status?
Response: Please note that temporary residents have an automatically imposed condition that they must leave Canada at the end of their authorized period of stay. However, as per section 181 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR), a temporary resident must apply to extend their period of authorized stay before it ends. If they have done so, their period of authorized stay as a temporary resident is extended by law until a decision is made R183(5). Such a person is considered to have legal status as a temporary resident during the processing period.
For additional information about automatic extension of status (formerly known as implied status), please visit our website.
If a couple is on study permit, can one discontinue studying and apply for open work permit? Does one spouse need to first change of status to visitor and then apply for SOWP?
Response: The spouse of a work permit holder may apply for a work permit while holding a valid study permit as it is possible for a foreign national to hold both a study permit and work permit simultaneously in some cases, as long as the client meets the eligibility requirements.
Please be advised that the assessment of an application is based on a case-by-case basis, considering the particular circumstances in conjunction with the supporting documentation available to the officer. The onus is always on the applicant to provide sufficient documentation to satisfy an officer that they meet the requirements.
For additional information about spousal work permits, please visit the immigration section of the Canada.ca website.
●For CEC applicants -- if one has Canadian work experience under two different NOCs; 6 months in A and 6 months in B category. Then how is lELTS considered because both categories have different bands requirements. For e.g. if the applicant gets bands for A (means higher bands), then he can surely apply. But if he gets bands for B category (means
lower bands), then he might have to work for 6 more months in B category and cannot use his lETLS to apply under CEC?
Response:
Pursuant to Section 87.1(2)(e) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations, the applicant must demonstrate that they meet the minimum language proficiency requirements for the occupational skill type/level in which they have obtained most (i.e., more than half) of their work experience.

If you plan to come to Canada as an international student after October 20, 2020: Your DLI must be on the list of DLIs with approved COVID-19 readiness plans before you travel to Canada.

This differs from the previous direction that 50% of each separate programs had to meet the PGWP requirement of being completed at least 50% in Canada.
NOTE: 50% of a total program of study is calculated based on the number of courses completed in Canada. Question: These days I am not receiving physical work permits. I get notices that they are approved, but nothing arrives in the mail. Is this something that is expected to change?
Response: Clients will only be mailed a physical work permit upon approval of their application if they applied in Canada using the form, Change Conditions, Extend My Stay or Remain in Canada as a Worker [IMM 5710]. The work permit will be mailed to the client's Canadian address on file. Please ensure that the address and contact information provided to IRCC is accurate and up-to-date. Clients may contact IRCC to update this information online or through our Web form.
If the client applies from outside of Canada using the form, Application for Work Permit Made Outside of Canada [IMM 1295], they will receive an approval letter (called the port of entry letter of introduction). Clients must present this letter at the port of entry when they arrive in Canada in order to be issued their physical work permit. If the client is currently inside Canada, but used the IMM 1295 form to submit their work permit application, the client will still only be issued a port of entry letter of introduction, not a physical work permit. Due to COVID-19 travel restrictions, clients who are unable to go to a port of entry to have their work permit issued may be eligible to have their work permit issued and mailed to them from within Canada. For more information on how to apply for this process, please see: Work permit: After you apply.

Answer:
The differing points grid in Express Entry was developed to reflect the increased economic success in Canada seen where the principal applicant has a spouse possessing certain competencies. IRCC does not support the use of these provisions in any kind of "strategic" way. We recommend that spouses who intend to live together in Canada, state that in their applications, and work to increase their CRS score while waiting in the pool for an invitation.
Changing the partner's status from "non-accompanying" to “accompanying" during the processing of an application, up to the time of landing, may not constitute misrepresentation; however, this choice was never intended to be used as a strategy. Rather, it allows families to accurately describe their situation and intentions and to comply with section 16 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act on the obligation to answer truthfully.

threads.subject: Fin du programme VIE et renouvellement du permis de travail via un code de dispense du PMI -- REP-2020- 1408
threads.question:
Tout d’abord, veuillez accepter nos excuses de cette réponse tardive.
Veuillez trouver ci-dessous nos réponses à vos questions.
Question 1:
Normalement dans le cadre du programme VIE, l’organisme responsable de la gestion du programme a la responsabilité de payer le salaire du TET. Toutefois, étant donné que le TET détient un permis de travail valide en faveur de notre client, est-ce que notre client peut rémunérer lui-même le TET entre le moment où l’organisme cessera de payer le salaire et la fin du permis de travail?
Réponse :
Oui. Les jeunes Français qui participent au programme VIE ne touchent ni salaire ni honoraires; Business France leur verse plutôt des appointements ou une allocation mensuelle directement en France. Cette allocation permet aux participants au programme VIE de maintenir des conditions de vie dans leur pays d’accueil, tout en maintenant des liens de résidence avec la France. Les participants au programme VIE doivent retourner en France après leur affectation. Business France garantit également que les participants au programme VIE ne seront pas un fardeau financier pour leur pays d’accueil en leur offrant un logement et en assumant tous leurs coûts associés aux services de santé.
Toutefois, si Business France a cessé de payer cette allocation et le permis de travail est valide et le travailleur ne peut pas retourner à son pays pendant la pandémie, l’employeur canadien pourra lui-même leur verser l’allocation mensuelle jusqu’à la fin du permis de travail.
Question 2 :
Normalement, l’employeur qui a soumis l’offre d’emploi dans le portail des employeur est responsable de De la même façon, puisque le travailleur étranger se retrouvera probablement en statut implicite, est-ce que notre client peut rémunérer lui-même le TET pendant la période de statut implicite?
Réponse :
Oui. Durant la pandémie, si le travailleur ne peut pas retourner à son pays, l’employeur peut continuer à payer le travailleur pendant la période de statut implicite.
Question 3 :
La Politique d’intérêt public visant les dispenses des conditions du permis de travail dans le cas d’un changement d’emploi en vigueur depuis le 12 mai 2020 prévoit qu’un TET au Canada qui change d’emploi ou d’employeur et qui a obtenu une offre d’emploi au titre du PMI ou du PTET peut demander une dispense via le formulaire Web d’IRCC. Est-ce que cette politique peut s’appliquer à un TET qui ne change ni d’employeur ni d’emploi, mais dont le salaire doit être payé par un autre organisme, en l’occurrence l’employeur inscrit à son permis de travail fermé au lieu de l’organisme responsable de la gestion du programme VIE?
Réponse :
Si le client a un permis de travail lié à un employeur donné et qu’il souhaite changer d’emploi ou d’employeur, il doit demander un nouveau permis de travail depuis le Canada. Les participants au Programme Expérience internationale Canada (EIC) doivent d'abord vérifier s'ils peuvent changer d’employeu' avec un permis de travail délivré dans le cadre d'EIC. Veuillez consulter : Prolongation de la durée de validité des permis de travail au titre du programme Expérience internationale Canada. Bien à vous,
Représentants immigration (IRCC)

In other words, can a foreign worker in self-quarantine work from home provided that they do not leave their premises or interact in person with others?
Answer Foreign workers who are in a 14-days quarantine period are allowed to telework as long as they are compliant with the Quarantine Act and the Public Health Agency of Canada's guidelines throughout the quarantine period. This is applicable if: the position and type of work are suitable for teleworking while respecting the Quarantine Act requirements;
- the work/tasks complies with what is stipulated in the employment contract or offer of employment for IMP; and,

As per subsection 73(1) of the Regulations, "Canadian educational credential" is defined as, "any secondary school diploma or any post-secondary diploma, certificate or credential that is issued on the completion of a Canadian program of study or training at an educational or training institution that is recognized by the provincial authorities responsible for registering, accrediting, supervising and regulating such institutions."

threads.subject: Dual Degree -- REP-2020-1917
threads.question:
Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox.
Question:
I have some clients who study overseas (no study permit) and obtain a dual degree for the same study from (a) their home country and (b) a Canadian University.
Are such degrees, considered as Canadian Degrees under the Express Entry program, even if the studies are abroad?
Answer:
Pursuant to Section 30(3) of the Ministerial Instructions respecting the Express Entry system, CRS points are only assigned under subsection (1) for Canadian educational credentials if, for the purpose of obtaining the credential, the foreign national
(a) studied in Canada at a Canadian educational institution;
(b) was enrolled in full-time study or training for at least eight months; and
(c) was physically present in Canada for at least eight months.
Officers must be satisfied that the credential meets these abovementioned requirements in order to be considered a Canadian educational credential. As this was not the case for this credential, to be awarded points for education, the applicant will need to get an educational credential equivalency assessment (ECA) in respect of their foreign educational
credentials issued by an organization or institution designated under subsection 75(4) of the Regulations.
We trust that this information will assist you.
Sincerely,
Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.subject: visitor applying for caregiver work permit -- REP-2020-2070
threads.question:
Dear
To respond to your question, a temporary public policy was issued on August 24, 2020, to allow certain temporary residents in Canada with valid visitor status to apply for an employer-specific work permit from within Canada, if they were in Canada on that date and remain in the country.
Under the caregiver Ministerial Instructions, the work permit refusal to process (RTP) only applies where all of the following conditions are met:
(a) the applicant is outside Canada;
(b) the applicant is making an initial work permit application (e.g. does not currently hold a valid work permit);
(c) the applicant intends to engage in work as described under National Occupation Classification (NOC) 4411 (excluding foster parents) and 4412 (excluding housekeepers);
(d) the applicant is destined to a job location outside Quebec; and
(e) the assessment, by Employment and Social Development Canada, and on the basis of which the officer must make a determination pursuant to paragraphs 203(1)(a) to (e) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations, was requested on or after June 18, 2019.
Therefore, for the duration that the public policy is in effect, visitors in Canada who meet all of the August 24 public policy eligibility requirements would not be subject to the work permit RTP for caregivers.
Thank you,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

Category B permanent residence application

threads.subject: URGENT-Question regarding work location -- REP-2020-2207
threads.question:
Hello,
If a holder of an open work permit identifies an "Employment Location" under the "Additional Information" section, but there is no "condition" or "remark" that states they are restricted from taking employment outside of the specified location, can the work permit holder work outside ofthe specified location?
This IRCC webpage refers only to co-op and postgraduate work permit holders. [https://www.cic.gc.ca/english/helpcentre/answer.asp?qnumn=1414&top=15](https://www.cic.gc.ca/english/helpcentre/answer.asp?qnumn=1414&top=15)
What about other types of open work permits, e.g. a spouse accompanying a skilled worker or student?
This is an urgent matter for my clients as they have job offers pending which could be affected by your answer.
Regards,
中 Citoenneté Canada
threads.answer:
Good day
A foreign worker must abide to all the conditions on his work permit, including the work location for their employment, as per sub-section R185(b)(iii) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations.
The work location on the work permit is entered as per the information provided under the Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) / letter of offer. If there are multiple locations indicated in the LMIA / offer of employment, the immigration will list them additional locations under the additional information section.
1. If the work permit received does not reflect the information enclosed within the LMIA or letter of employment, the applicant must submit a request to Amend Valid Temporary Resident Documents or Information Contained in the Confirmation of Permanent Residence.
2.If the information on the work permit is accurate but the foreign national obtained a new LMlA or letter of employment to work at a different location, the applicant must submit a request to Extend or change the conditions on your work permit
This information is valid for all types of work permits.
We trust you will find this information useful.
Regards,

( ) ## # Hello,
QUESTION: When an applicant is in Canada in implied status and their PR application is approved, should the pending Work Permit application be withdrawn through the representative's online account? Does withdrawing the application invalidate their previous implied status in any way? Or, should a Web Form just be submitted to advise IRCC that the person has become a PR?
RESPoNSE: For a foreign national to become a permanent resident in Canada, they must first be a temporary resident. A temporary resident has their status extended automatically by law when they submit an application for an extension of their period of authorized stay prior to the expiry of their present status. The period of authorized stay is extended pending a decision. Upon withdrawal, the applicant no longer has a pending application under R181, and therefore, no longer meets the requirements of R183(5). In your scenario, the application would have the status of temporary resident until the withdrawal is registered.
For efficiency, it is recommended that a Web Form be submitted to flag that the work permit applicant is now a permanent resident. The work permit application will be refused or you may withdraw it. Since the withdrawal will be made after the person has become a permanent resident it should not affect their previous auto-extended period of stay (implied status).

threads.subject: Study permit application under IRPR 215(1)(f)(i)--REP-2020-1579
threads.question:
Good day,
Apologies for the delayed response. As per Section 30(2) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA), [e]very minor child in Canada, other than a child of a temporary resident not authorized to work or study, is authorized to study at the pre-school, primary or secondary level. This means that the child of a visitor (i.e., not authorized to work or study) may not study in Canada without a study permit.
Additionally, as per Paragraph 188(1)(c) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR), [a] foreign national may study in Canada without a study permit if the duration of their course or program of studies is six months or less and will be completed within the period for their stay authorized upon entry into Canada. In the context of primary and secondary level of study, this exemption applies if the foreign national plans to complete the program that is less than 6 months in duration. With regard to the scenario described in your email since the length of a school year program is more than six months, the child is not exempt from the study permit requirement under Paragraph 188(1)(c)
Please note R215(1)(f)(i) applies to those study permit holders already in Canada who may wish to apply for another study permit for a different level of study or apply for an extension to their current study permit.
Thank you,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

This is a response to your inquiry about the 2-stage process and international student's eligibility to work. As a facilitation measure to support the fall 2020 intake of international students, the department-implemented a temporary 2-stage assessment process for initial study permit applications for applicants who were outside of Canada. The 2-stage process did not apply to in-Canada study permit extension applications. This temporary 2-stage assessment process for study permit applications consisted of eligibility and admissibility assessments.
Officers made a stage-one preliminary eligibility assessment based on the information on file. If the applicant met all stage one requirements, they received a positive stage one assessment. However, the positive stage one assessment is not a valid study permit, nor does it guarantee that the study permit application would be approved.
In order for international students to be eligible to work in Canada for up to 20 hours a week while in class in session, students must have a valid study permit, be a full-time student and be enrolled at a DLl.

threads.subject: Submitting a new work permit application while in implied status -- REP-2020-2390
threads.question:
Dear Officer,
I am seeking guidance regarding how to tackle a situation where a temporary foreign worker on an open work permit: 1) submits
and Citizenshi Canada et Ciloyeneé Canada
an application to extend their work permit for a relatively short period of time that is less than the time anticipated to process the application (e.g. to get the complete validity period of a work permit where the initial validity was limited by the expiration date of the applicant's passport); 2) would like to submit a second application for a work permit for a named employer.
In the past, we have seen that where a decision is rendered on an application to extend an open work permit AFTER the requested end date for the work permit requested, the decision is a refusal. An application made after the refusal would normally have to be an application for restoration of status which would, at a minimum, lead to a prolonged period where the applicant could not work and, in some other cases (e.g. A75) preclude the subsequent application altogether. In this situation, would it be possible to submit an application for a work permit for a particular employer prior the expiry of the period requested for the validity of the work permit on a prior application which is still in process? If so, what is the mechanism through which this can be accomplished?
Thank you in advance for your feedback and assistance.
Sincerely,
threads.answer:
Hello,
QuESTioN: Is it possible to submit an application for a work permit for a particular employer prior the expiry of the period requested for the validity of the work permit on a prior application which is still in process? If so, what is the mechanism through which this can be accomplished?
RESPoNSE: A person who submits a renewal of their work permit under R201 will then be eligible to work without a permit under R186(u) until a decision is made on the renewal application. If during the processing period of the application while the person is working under the authority of R186, they wish to submit a new work permit application (ie: after the exisiting work permit expired but during processing period) for the new employer specific work permit. They may submit the second application from within Canada under the authority of R199(b) as they are working without a permit under R186(u).

threads.subject: Implied Status clarification -- REP-2020-2399
threads.question:
Dear Sir, Madam,
I hope this email finds you well.
After submitting work permit extensions within Canada, we have been receiving the following message from IRCC for all of our clients:
Please attach this letter to your present work permit Numberas proof that you
are authorized to continue working with the same conditions (ie: employer and occupation) until
March 24, 2021or until a decision is made on your application, whichever is first. This extended period of work is authorized as per subsection 186(u) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations. If you leave Canada before a decision is made on your application, you
will no longer be authorized to continue working.
Our concern is whether IRCC has changed policies regarding implied status. According to IRPR 183 (5):
(5) Subject to subsection (5.1), if a temporary resident has applied for an extension of the period authorized for their stay and a decision is not made on the application by the end of the period authorized for their stay, the period is extended until
- (a) the day on which a decision is made, if the application is refused; or
- (b) the end of the new period authorized for their stay, if the application is allowed.
Regulation 186(u), as mentioned in IRCC's letter states:
186 A foreign national may work in Canada without a work permit
(u) until a decision is made on an application made by them under subsection 201(1), if they have remained in Canada after the expiry of their work permit and they have continued to comply with the conditions set out on the expired work permit, other than the expiry date;
As such, an applicant has always maintained implied status until the day a decision is rendered on their work permit extension, whenever that may be. However the letters from IRCC seem to imply that the period of implied status will end on a specific date determined by IRCC (in this case March 24, 2021) and not when a decision is rendered on the case.
Linmdi So we are asking for clarification as to whether an applicant does maintain implied status until a decision is rendered or if there is a new IRCC policy stating the implied status will end before a decision has been rendered.
Thank you for claryfing.
Sincerely,
threads.answer:
Hello,
QUESTioN: So we are asking for clarification as to whether an applicant does maintain implied status until a decision is rendered or if there is a new IRCC policy stating the implied status will end before a decision has been rendered.
RESPONSE: The status in not 'implied' but maintained if the application is submitted prior to the expiry of their existing status. Yes, you are correct in that the Regulations state that the period of authorized stay is extended until a decision is made and that a person who is applying to renew their work permit will have authority to work under R186(u) until a decision is made unless they leave Canada.
The letter is provided to applicants as proof that they have continued authority to work unless they leave Canada and the date is added to give employers and other stakeholders a more concrete period of time of authorized work. IRCC has found in the past that employers and stakeholders are reluctant to accept an unknown period such as 'until a decision is made'. Should the application not be processed within the date on the letter clients may contact IRCC using the IRCC Web form to request continued proof. In addition, there is no legal requirement that the applicant must present this letter to anyone it is only provided as a service to the client.
The letter has a 120 validity that corresponds with IRCC Service Standard for in-Canada applications. Historically, IRCC meets our service standard more than 90% of the time. During the initial COVID-19 pandemic period the processing time has gone beyond our service standard. However, IRCC has been working to reduce our current processing time back to the service standard by the time that the first letters will be expiring (ie: February 2021) IRCC will again be processing within the Service Standard.
The letter also indicates that : This extended period of work is authorized as per subsection 186(u) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations. This statement would provide the evidence that they can continue working until a decision is made.
For clarity: the applicant may continue working until a decision is made if they meet all the requirements of R186(u) regardless of the date in the letter. The letter is simply a document to provide surety to employers and other stakeholders that the applicant may continue working.
