threads.subject: Residency requirement clarification -- REP-2020-0375
threads.question:
Good afternoon,
Thank you for your question,
A permanent resident may be away from Canada for three years in every five-year period, for any reason, and be in compliance with the residency obligation. Accordingly, if the applicant satisfies an officer that they have been physically present in Canada for at least 730 days in the five-year period being examined, it is not necessary to examine or assess
other factors regarding the reason for the absence.
If the absence was due to employment abroad, the burden of proof rests with the applicant to provide information and evidence to satisfy an officer that their employment abroad is in compliance with the regulatory description of the R61(3) qualifying criteria for employment abroad and the R61(1) definition of a "Canadian business".
1. How a full-time employment is paid is not part of the description of a full-time employment. As long as the PR is working full-time and satisfies an officer that is employment abroad is in compliance with the regulatory, the qualifying criteria for employment abroad and definition of a "Canadian business" the time spent outside Canada would probably count.
2. Maternity is considered as a leave and can't be considered as a full-time employment. Based on R61(3), someone on maternity leave would not be entitled to count this time spent outside Canada.
Thank you,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

2) Full time students who hold a valid study permit and who have begun their studies can work off campus provided they meet the eligibility criteria;
- Note that off campus work is limited to 20 hours per week during the regular school terms and full time during scheduled breaks.

They may work a total of 20 hours per week including both the hours for the co-op placement and the hours at other part-time jobs (if they have one). They must stop their co-op placement immediately if the application is refused.

threads.subject: Interim Pathway for Caregivers-Closed -- REP-2020-2195
threads.question:
Dear
Thank you for contacting the Immigration Representative Mailbox.
A temporary resident must apply to extend their period of authorized stay before it ends. If they have done so, their period of authorized stay as a temporary resident is extended by law until a decision is made [R183(5)]. Such a person is considered to have maintained their status (sometimes referred to as implied status) as a temporary resident during that period.
If a temporary resident applies for renewal of their work or study permit and their permit expires before a decision is made, paragraph 186(u) and section 189 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR) (the right to continue working or studying under the same conditions pending a determination of their application for renewal) apply only as long as the person remains in Canada.
Individuals who are on temporary status in Canada may consider submitting a separate work permit application or an extension of their existing work permit under the Temporary Foreign Worker Program (TFWP) or the International Mobility Program (IMP), even if they have applied for the Interim Pathway for Caregivers.
It is important to note that a temporary public policy was issued to exempt temporary foreign workers from certain requirements when they are changing employment and remains in effect until it is revoked by the Minister of and Citizenship. The public policy allows temporary foreign workers already in Canada to more quickly begin work in advance of a final decision on their employer-specific work permit application, provided that they:
a. are changing jobs or employers, and
b. have secured a job offer under the terms of either the Temporary Foreign Worker Program or the International Mobility Program
Please see here for more information on the new public policy. This means that caregivers who are seeking to obtain or extend their LMIA-required work permit under the TFWP may be eligible for consideration under the new public policy if they are applying for another employer-specific work permit and are changing employment. The public policy does not apply to open work permit holders.
Note that work permit applications for caregivers under the TFWP, that are not submitted as part of a permanent residence application, are currently part of the COVID-19 prioritization list for faster processing; for more information, please refer to Work permit: COVID-19 program delivery.
We trust this information will assist you.
Sincerely, The Immigration Representative Mailbox

Good day,
This is in response to your inquiry sent on September 24, 2020 regarding additional clarification on co-op work permit.
The co-op work permit and the off-campus work authorization listed on the study permit serve different purposes and are not interchangeable. In other word, international students must obtain their valid co-op work permit prior to starting their work terms. The designated learning institution (DLl) should clearly establish that the work is an essential part of the academic, vocational or professional training program that all participants enrolled in the program are required to complete in order to receive their degree, diploma or certificate. If students won't exceed 20 hours of off-campus work per week during a regular academic session, they may use the work authorizations of their study permit to complete co-op work while waiting for the decision of their co-op work permit application. Please note, in order to use their study permit work authorizations to work in health or early childhood program, the study permit must not include the restriction to work in in such fields: “Not authorized to work in 1) child care, 2) primary or secondary school teaching, 3) health services field occupations". However, if their co-op work permit application is refused, the students would not be allowed to continue their co-op program without authorization.
I trust this information is of assistance to you,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox
threads.answer:
Good Afternoon
Thank you for your inquiry.
Both a co-op work permit as well as a study permit are required when International Students are enrolled in an
academic, professional or vocational training program at a designated learning institution that requires mandatory
work experience, such as a co-op or internship placement as part of their program requirements.
If completing the internship requires them to work less than 20 hours per week during the academic schedule or full time during the summer break they are still required to secure a co-op work permit.
To get a co-op work permit, the student must prove that the work experience/internship is essential to successful completion of their program. Acceptable proof of this requirement may include a letter from the school they are attending or a copy of the school curriculum.
Please note however that the co-op or internship/work experience requirement cannot be more than 50% of the total program of study. Also note that Foreign nationals studying English or French as a second language (ESL/FSL), or participating in general interest or preparatory courses, are not eligible for a co-op work permit.
There is no fee for the co-op work permit. For more information, see Work permits for students-Co-op and internship programs.

RESPONSE: Le travailleur spécialisé diffère des postes de direction, en ce sens qu'un travailleur spécialisé doit posséder un niveau élevé de connaissances spécialisées, ce qui est rare dans un secteur particulier, alors le salaire ou le traitement doit être conforme à ce spécialiste. Un tel spécialiste percevrait généralement un salaire supérieur à la moyenne; par conséquent, un plancher salarial fixé aux niveaux de salaire en vigueur constituera une base de référence pour l'évaluation de ces demandes.
Les agents détermineront le salaire en vigueur au Canada pour la profession et la région de travail spécifiques en utilisant l'outil du site web "Travailler au Canada" d'Emploi et Développement social Canada (ESDC) pour déterminer le salaire canadien en vigueur.
Pour les postes de direction, il n'y a pas de critère salarial fixé. Les agents examineront les cas sur une base individuelle et conformément aux normes salariales de la province où le demandeur est destiné.
Veuillez noter que ce service a pour but de fournir des orientations fonctionnelles générales, et que nous ne sommes donc pas en mesure de fournir des conseils spécifiques à un cas particulier. Veuillez noter que l'évaluation d'une demande se fait au cas par cas, en tenant compte des circonstances particulières en conjonction avec les pièces justificatives dont dispose l'agent. Il incombe toujours au demandeur de fournir des documents suffisants pour convaincre l'agent qu'il satisfait aux exigences.
Veuillez référer aux instructions suivantes: o Cadre de direction et gestionnaires principaux o Gestionnaires fonctionnels o Travailleurs qui possèdent des connaissances spécialisées

Question:
- A PR application (along with her OWP application) was submitted and received last Oct 3, 2019 under the Interim Pathway for Caregivers. On the 89th day after work permit expired, a restoration of status was applied to a request to change into a visitor. Now that she is a visitor record holder as of Oct 20, 2020 Will the visitor record document supercedes the implied status? Response:
R186(u) allows temporary residents to work without a work permit, if
- they have applied to renew their work permit under R201 before the original work permit expired;
- they have remained in Canada, and;
- they continue to continue to comply with the conditions set out on the expired work permit, other than the expiry date. Paragraph R183(5) grants an extension of temporary resident status by operation of law, commonly known as ‘implied status.'
It is not the automatic extension (commonly known as “implied status’) under subsection R183(5) that authorizes a temporary resident to continuing working while their application for an extension of their work permit is in progress. The temporary resident must meet the requirements of paragraph R186(u) to continue working. Paragraph R186(u) applies only until a decision is made on the original work permit renewal application
A temporary resident who submits the form “Application to change conditions, extend my stay or remain in Canada as a Worker" [IMM 5710] to renew their work permit is in fact submitting two applications in one. The temporary resident is applying under section R181 for an “extension of temporary resident status" and under section R201 to “renew the work permit". If submitted before the expiry of their current work permit, this combined application has three effects:
mmigration, Refugees
- Should a final decision not be made on the application under section R181 before the expiration of their present status, the foreign national will be allowed to remain by operation of law (implied status) under subsection R183(5).
- The application for renewal under section R201 triggers the ability for the foreign national to “work without a work permit" under paragraph R1 86(u) until a decision is made, unless they leave Canada.
- Any conditions imposed on the current work permit carry over into the implied status period under paragraph R1 86(u). For example, a holder of an employer-specific work permit may only continue to work for the same employer/location whereas the holder of an open work permit may continue to work for any employer with no restrictions on location until the decision is made on the renewal of the work permit.
If a foreign national made an application to renew their work permit authorization (used IMM 5710 application form) before their initial work permit expired, the above guidance would apply. The foreign national would not have lost their status if their work permit expired—their status was maintained under R183(5). As a result, the applicant is not required to submit an application to restore their status under R182 Restoration ofTemporary Resident Status.
If a foreign national—who maintained their status as a TR under R183(5)—made an application to restore their status as temporary resident, and received a positive decision on their application for restoration, they are no longer on implied status under R183(5) (as they have a visitor record); however, they would still be able to continue working with their initial employer without work permit under R186(u) under the same conditions until a decision is made on their application for renewal under section R201.
If the foreign national's initial employer terminated their contract, and the applicant found a new employer, and received an offer of employment to work with an employer-specific work permit (with an LMIA), the caregiver may benefit from one of the public policies announced by IRCC during the Covid-19 pandemic until a decision is made on their OWP application under the interim pathway for caregivers.

Please note that the issuance of Medical Instructions (IMM1017) is under the delegation and responsibility of the immigration officers. However please note that once medical instructions are issued to applicants an IME# is subsequently generated in GCMS and eMedical (system used by panel physician). That said, should an IME remain inactive for a certain period (15 months) it is then purged from eMedical and physicians can no longer use it. Should the client still visit a panel clinic and use the outdated form, the PP can create an Upfront exam if they are unable to locate the IME in eMedical (due to purge). The Upfront IME would be sent to GCMS but would not be associated to the UCl and would require that the officer complete an integrated search for a T# in order to locate the results.
Unfortunately, without knowing when the letter was issued to an applicant then it would be difficult to determine if an outdate letter can be used as this is tied to an IME# in GCMS and eMedical. threads.subject: C-16 Inquiry -- REP-2020-2437
threads.question: From Dear Agent, Kindly advise on the following question: In the context of the C-16 (francophone) application. Is the applicant required to meet the prevailing wage for the NOC? Thank you in advance for your response. Sincerely,
threads.answer:
Immigration Representatives / Représentants inmigration (IRCC)
Thank you for your question. In the context of the C-16 (francophone) application. Is the applicant required to meet the prevailing wage for the NOC? Response: The general criteria under the LMIA exemption code C16 (Mobilité Francophone) are: 1-The employer must submit an Offer of Employment, as per section R209.11, before a work permit application is made. 2-Officers should apply the LMIA exemption code C16 to work permit applications received on or after June 1, 2016, if they are satisfied that the foreign national is
- destined to work in a province or territory outside Quebec
- qualified to work in managerial, professional, technical or skilled trades occupations (NOC 0, A or B)
The prevailing wage for the NOC 0 or A is not a requirement under the LMIA-exemption code C16. It should be noted that the employer is subject to comply with the following conditions under R209.2.
1. The employer must comply with the federal and provincial laws that regulate employment and the recruiting of employees in the province in which the foreign national works [R209.2(1)(a)(ii)].
2. The employer must provide the foreign worker with employment in the same occupation as that set out in the offer of employment and with wages and working conditions that are substantially the same as, but not less favourable than, those in the same offer [R209.2(1)(a)(ii]. [...]
Regards, The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.subject: GTS LMIA and Work Permit Duration -- REP-2020-2456
threads.question:
Dear IRCC
Are you able to shed light on this question?
An employer obtained a GTS LMA that was issued for a 3 year duration, though I note that ESDC policy is that these LMIAs should only be issued for 2 years.
The individual employee then used this LMIA and applied for a work permit online, and was issued a work permit approval letter by IRCC valid for only 2 years. CBSA issued the work permit on arrival for about 2 years.
Does this mean that he cannot apply for one more year of work permit, based on the LMIA?
Many thanks in advance.
threads.answer:
Hello,
Thank you for contacting the Immigration Representatives mailbox. We are unable to respond to case-specific enquiries, but encourage you to contact the appropriate resources below.
The expectation is that the CBSA and IRCC officers will issue a work permit for the duration of work indicated in the LMlA. However, in the case of passport expiry, a work permit may be issued for a shorter duration than identified in the LMIA. For example, if the LMIA work duration is for two years, but the temporary foreign worker's passport will expire in one year, then the officer will issue a work permit for one year.
In cases of passport expiry only, provided the initial LMIA and WP application were received before the LMIA expiry date, temporary foreign workers will be able to renew their existing work permit at the CPC-Edmonton, without seeking a new LMIA. That is, while the expiry date of the LMIA will have passed, the temporary foreign worker met the initial time frame for the application and can therefore be extended up until the end of the duration time outlined in the initial LMIA, provided the passport has been renewed accordingly.

Question: can you please advise whether applicants under the Spouse-in-Canada sponsorship class are eligible for an open work permit if they are out of status and eligible for restoration under the new public policy extending the restoration period beyond 90 days and to the end of December 2020?
Response: As stated in the program delivery instructions: the public policy introduces an exemption from the requirement to apply for restoration within 90 days of losing temporary resident status for all foreign nationals (former workers, students and visitors) in Canada. Question 1:

Can the foreign national update the pending work permit application to request and receive consideration under the new policy (i.e. via Case Specific Enquiry) or will the foreign national be required to submit a new work permit application under the policy and withdraw the application for work permit made outside Canada that is already in process?
1. Response:
Please note that this service is to give general functional guidance, thus we are not able to provide case-specific advice. Foreign nationals who applied for a work permit (using the IMM 1295 form – Application for Work Permit Made Outside Canada) may be eligible for an interim work authorization while awaiting a decision on a pending work permit application if they meet all the eligibility requirements of the public policy. That is, the foreign national must: have been in Canada on August 24, 2020, and have remained in Canada since,
have and maintain valid temporary resident status,

In general, IRCC strongly recommends that applicants requesting consideration under the public policy use the
Application to Change Conditions or Extend Your Stay in Canada [IMM 5710] for the following reasons: Under the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and Regulations, foreign nationals who are temporary residents in Canada are required to maintain valid TR status in Canada for the duration of their stay, including until a decision is made on their work permit application.
- As it stands, foreign nationals who submit the IMM 5710 form (in Canada application form to extend/renew work permit) are considered to be simultaneously applying for work authorization and temporary resident
Lnmn status. Therefore, the period of their authorized stay as a TR will be extended by operation of law under R183(5), and they retain their status, subject to any other conditions imposed, during the extended period.
However, foreign nationals who submit a new work permit application using the IMM 1295 (outside of Canada application form) while in Canada, are not considered to be applying for temporary resident status at the same time, and therefore do not benefit from the continuation of status and conditions under R183(5), even if the work permit application was made before the expiry of their authorized stay.
If their application was submitted to a Migration Office, they will have to submit a separate application to extend their temporary resident status in Canada and pay additional fees.

Canada are processed as per the priority of the Migration office. Only the decision on interim work authorization will be made within 30 business days.

was initially granted to them by the border services officer at a port of entry.

The instruction guide is correct. A Japanese citizen who is currently in Canada and on a valid Visitor Record, will not need to provide their biometrics for a visitor extension request (subject to IRPA or IRPR A16(2)).
The reason being, some foreign nationals (FNs) come from a visa-exempt country and only require an Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA) to come to Canada. Given that Japan is one of said countries, and your client is a Japanese
national visiting Canada; they were most likely admitted into Canada with an eTA.
FN's who require an eTA to enter and/or remain in Canada as visitors are exempt from the biometrics requirement. However, a visa-exempt FNs applying for a study or work permit will be required to provide biometrics.
Furthermore, FN's from visa-required countries who have provided their biometrics in a previous Temporary Resident (TR) applications (study, work or visitors) do not need to re-enroll their biometrics before the 10 year
validity period (i.e. the date of enrollment plus ten years).
Should a Biometric Instruction Letter (BIL) be issued for any subsequent TR application (including Temporary Resident Visas (TRVs), work and study permits (WP & SP), visitor records (VRs), Temporary Resident Permits (TRPs) and extensions), please ensure that the client self-discloses their eligibility for a biometrics exemption, under the 1 in 10 policy, either online or in person.

To further add, the period of allowable stay in Canada cannot exceed the remaining validity of the applicant's biometrics. Applicants may choose to voluntarily re-enroll their biometrics and pay the required fee before the end of the 10-year period, which allows applicants to apply for a visa that extends beyond their current biometric validity. For example, applicants who want to apply for a new 10-year visa, and who last enrolled their biometrics 8 years ago, can obtain a visa for a maximum of only 2 years. threads.answer:
updated version ofIMM5988 -- REP-2020-2471
Attachments: IMM5988_blacked out.pdf,
Hello,
QUESTION: We would respectfully ask that this new letter is reviewed as it is incorrect. Once an applicant is in implied status under R186(u) they are permitted to continue working “..until a decision is made on an application made by them under subsection 201(1), if they have remained in Canada after the expiry of their work permit and they have continued to comply with the conditions set out on the expired work permit, other than the expiry date". The attached letter indicates that an applicant's ability to work will end on a certain date that may arrive prior to a decision on an application. It should be amended to clearly reflect that an applicant can continue to work until a decision is rendered and not until a specific date.
RESPONSE: The status in not 'implied' but maintained if the application is submitted prior to the expiry of their existing status. Yes, you are correct in that the Regulations state that the period of authorized stay is extended until a decision is made and that a person who is applying to renew their work permit will have authority to work under R186(u) until a decision is made unless they leave Canada.
The letter is provided to applicants as proof that they have continued authority to work unless they leave Canada and the date is added to give employers and other stakeholders a more concrete period of time of authorized work. IRCC has found in the past that employers and stakeholders are reluctant to accept an unknown period such as 'until a decision is made'. Should the application not be processed within the date on the letter clients may contact IRCC using the IRCC Web form to request continued proof. threads.subject: Questions on News Release on July 14, 2020-Ottawa--REP-2020-1828
threads.question:
Dear sir/madam,
This email is regarding the news that Minister Mendicino announces changes to facilitate online learning for international students.
"The new measures include
- providing priority study-permit processing for students who have submitted a complete application online, to ensure that permits are processed as quickly as possible
- allowing students to count the time spent pursuing their studies online abroad toward their eligibility for a post-graduation work permit, if they have submitted a study permit application and if at least 50% of their program is completed in Canada
- providing reassurances to international students who cannot submit all of the documentation needed to complete
Citoyenneté Canada
processing of their applications, and who choose to pursue programs through distance learning, by implementing a temporary 2-stage approval process The temporary process will allow applicants to count the time spent studying online abroad towards their post-graduation work permit once they receive an approval-in-principle, as long as they are able to satisfy all requirements and receive the full approval of their study permit application at a later date. As services begin to reopen, applicants will be required to submit remaining documents and receive an approved study permit before being allowed to travel to Canada.
This process is available to students starting a program in the fall semester who submit a study permit application before September 15, 2020. This measure will reassure students that they can enrol and begin their studies this fall online, even when
they are not able to submit all required documentation due to pandemic-related closures."
My question is whether international students in the following situation also apply to the measures above:
1. Students starting a program in the fall semester have submitted the study permit application of outside Canada type before September 15, 2020, and are currently residing inside Canada.
2. Students holding a valid post graduate work permit have submitted the study permit application from inside Canada before September 15, 2020, and are currently residing inside Canada.
Are these students allowed to start their fall semester before the approval of their study permit application?
Thanks for your time on this question.
Look forward to hearing from you soon.
Best regards,
Citoyenneté Canada
threads.answer:
Good day,
Thank you for your inquiry.
The 2-stage assessment process for study permit applications only applies to initial study permit applications made outside of Canada and does not apply to in-Canada study permit applications. Students may begin a program via distance learning from outside Canada without a study permit, as a study permit is not required for this type of program. The facilitative measure was introduced in response to travel restrictions as a result of COVID-19 and allows this time spent studying before an approval is received to count towards a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP).
A study permit is still required for programs inside Canada which are normally offered in-person but have moved to an online format due to COVID-19, unless they are shorter than 6 months in duration and therefore exempt from requiring a study permit under R188. Therefore, a foreign national may not begin studying inside Canada without a study permit, even if they have already submitted an application.
The foreign nationals in question would therefore not be able to begin studying without a study permit, unless they had applied prior to the expiry of a previous study permit and therefore benefit from maintaining their status, or if the program falls under R188 and no study permit is required.
I trust this information is of assistance to you,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.subject: Study permit for minors in Canada-Clarification-Urgent--REP-2020-1779
threads.question:
Good day,
As per Section 30(2) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA), [e]very minor child in Canada, other than a child of a temporary resident not authorized to work or study, is authorized to study at the pre-school, primary or secondary level. This means that the child of a visitor (i.e., not authorized to work or study) may not study in Canada without a study permit.
Additionally, as per Paragraph 188(1)(c) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR), [a] foreign national may study in Canada without a study permit if the duration of their course or program of studies is six months or less and will be completed within the period for their stay authorized upon entry into Canada. In the context of primary and secondary level of study, this exemption applies if the foreign national plans to complete the program that is less than six months in duration.
If a minor child is in Canada as a visitor and their parents don't have a work or study permit, and wish to study in Canada more than six months, they must make an application from outside Canada
Please note R215(1)(f)(i) applies to those study permit holders already in Canada who may wish to apply for another study permit for a different level of study or apply for an extension to their current study permit.

A temporary resident must apply to extend their period of authorized stay before it ends. If they have done so, their period of authorized stay as a temporary resident is extended by law until a decision is made [R183(5)]. Such a person is considered to have maintained their status (sometimes referred to as implied status) as a temporary resident during that period.
If a temporary resident applies for renewal of their work or study permit and their permit expires before a decision is made, paragraph 186(u) and section 189 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR) (the right to continue working or studying under the same conditions pending a determination of their application for renewal) apply only as long as the person remains in Canada.
Individuals who are on temporary status in Canada may consider submitting a separate work permit application or an extension of their existing work permit under the Temporary Foreign Worker Program (TFWP) or the International Mobility Program (IMP),even if they have already applied under the Home Child Care Provider/Home Support Worker pilots. Please refer to Work permit: COVID-19 program delivery for additional information.
It is important to note that a temporary public policy was issued to exempt temporary foreign workers from certain requirements when they are changing employment and remains in effect until it is revoked by the Minister of and Citizenship. threads.question:
Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox.
Question:
I am seeking clarification about work experience factors under the Canadian Express Class and Foreign Skilled Worker. Please see below.
1) Please confirm whether a foreign national performing activities in Canada at a Canadian institution with a payee from outside Canada (including Government authorities) would meet the eligibility criteria of the Canadian work experience under the Canadian Experience Class. Please note that, sometimes foreign workers cannot submit a NOA, T4 or paystubs from Canada, but it is able to demonstrate that the work is remunerated and performed in Canada.
2) Please confirm whether the employer must be Canadian and/or the remuneration for the work performed in Canada must be in Canadian dollars in order to meet the eligibility criteria of the Canadian experience class.
3) Please confirm if currently there is any restricted occupation listed by the Minister.
4) Please confirm whether military services (either soldier on the field or other positions working for the military of a Government) is restricted to use as foreign work experience under the Canadian Experience Class and Federal Skilled Worker.
Answer:
1) It is not the location of the employer that determines whether or not the applicant will be attributed points for Canadian work experience. If the applicant was authorized to work in Canada, was not self-employed, had TR status, and was not a full-time student, then their work experience in Canada could count for the purposes of accumulating CRS points for Canadian Work Experience. In addition, the applicant must meet all the other requirements of section 15 of the MI's.
2) No, there are no restricted occupations listed by the Minister for Permanent Resident Applications.
3) Military services (either soldier on the field or other positions working for the military of a Government) are not restricted to use as foreign work experience under the Canadian Experience Class and Federal Skilled Worker. The applicant may select the most similar NOC to the work experience that they have acquired.
In all cases, the onus is on the applicant to establish that they meet the CEC program criteria at the time of their application. All applicants are required to provide satisfactory evidence of their work experience in Canada, including the fact that they were in an employer-employee relationship during their period of qualifying work experience.

threads.subject: Remote working possible for C16 work permit? -- REP-2020-1434
threads.question:
Hello,
Under most circumstances, there is no restriction against a foreign worker working remotely from their home in Canada, provided the job offer is in support of a Canadian employer physically located in Canada. For example, if a NAFTA Computer Systems Analyst has a job offer from an employer based in Toronto but will be working from their residence in Nova Scotia, this is typically permitted, and "Toronto" would be listed as the foreign worker's place of employment on their work permit.
I have three questions regarding remote working and specifically, the C16 - Francophone mobility category:
- In the case of a work permit based on the C16 - Francophone mobility category, could you please advise whether working remotely is possible from an immigration perspective?
- If yes, may the foreign worker work from their residence in Quebec, if the job offer is based in a province other than Quebec?
- Please advise whether specific mention of remote working is required in the online offer of employment submitted to IRCC, for all work permit categories under the IMP, in order for the employer to remain compliant with IRCC requirements.
Thank you very much. I look forward to your response.
Kind regards,
threads.answer:
Hello,
Our sincere apologies for not responding sooner. Please find below our response to your questions.
Question:
1. In the case of a work permit based on the C16 - Francophone mobility category, could you please advise whether working remotely is possible from an immigration perspective?
2. If yes, may the foreign worker work from their residence in Quebec, if the job offer is based in a province other than Quebec? Response: Working remotely under C16 (teleworking) in Quebec (Questions 1 &2) Under the LMIA-exemption code C16, the majority of the professional activities should be done outside of Quebec. The examples stated below may be acceptable as long as they are incidental/exceptional to the foreign national's main duties and are unanticipated or temporary in nature. Note that the employer must provide the foreign worker with employment in the same occupation as that set out in the offer of employment and with wages and working conditions that are substantially the same as, but not less favorable than, those in the same offer. Here are some examples of activities that would be allowed under the C-16 work permit category:
a. The Foreign national is based outside of Quebec, but needs to attend a conference in Quebec.
b. The Foreign national is based outside of Quebec, but from time to time has to visit Quebec based customers of the employer for business meetings.
The policy intent of the C16 LMIA-exemption is to encourage the development of minority official language communities in Canada. Promoting the use of French outside Quebec strengthens and supports the social and cultural fabric of Canadian society, while respecting the federal, bilingual and multicultural character of Canada. As stated above, while it is not prohibited to conduct some professional activities in Quebec, the foreign national should work most of the time outside of Quebec. For example, it would be against the policy intent to telework from, or work in
Quebec on a regular basis.
In the context of Covid-19 pandemic:
Workers entering Canada through the Temporary Foreign Worker (TFW) or International Mobility (IMP) Programs must fulfill their obligations as outlined under Orders made pursuant to the Quarantine Act. In particular, workers must quarantine themselves for the first 14 days upon arrival to Canada, unless they are deemed to be providing an essential service by the Chief Public Health Officer of Canada.
mmigration, Réfugiés
While in quarantine, workers must adhere to the measures put in place by Public Health Agency Canada (PHAC). Employers must not do anything that would prevent workers from complying with orders or regulations under the Quarantine Act and/or the Emergencies Act. Preventing workers from complying includes not enabling the workers to be in mandatory quarantine/isolation upon their entry to Canada.
Teleworking during quarantine is allowed if the worker is compliant with the Quarantine Act and PHAC guidelines throughout the quarantine period. This would apply specifically if:
- the position and type of work are suitable for teleworking while respecting the Quarantine Act requirements;
- the work/tasks complies with what is stipulated in the employment contract or offer of employment for IMP; and,
- the TFW has the equipment to perform their work from their quarantine location.
Question 3: Please advise whether specific mention of remote working is required in the online offer of employment s ubmitted to IRCC, for all work permit categories under the IMP, in order for the employer to remain compliant with IRCC requirements. Response
The regulatory framework of significant benefit (R205) is structured around the work the individual will perform, which in this case, must be in a non-francophone community outside of Quebec.
C16 applicants must work outside of Quebec as that's the parameter we actually require in order for the foreign worker to be eligible for a C16 work permit.
If the client is teleworking as part of the 14-day quarantine or PHAC directives, then the employers don't need to mention it in the Offer of Employment. If the teleworking is not part of the 14-day quarantine, the employers should mention (percentage of total work) it in their offer of employment.

Answer: If a husband and wife are listed on the commitment certificate and are part of the team, then two applications must be submitted, as the document checklist indicates. This includes both essential and non-essential business applicants. Applicants would only be on the same application if one spouse was not on the team. As of June 1, 2014, foreign nationals who are studying at the preschool, primary or secondary level [R215(1)(f)(i)], or who are a visiting or exchange student at a DLI [R215(1)(f)(ii)], may apply for a study permit from within Canada. The applicant must provide a letter of acceptance from the DLI at which they are enrolled or will be enrolled.
Visiting students are students who have been admitted to a post-secondary institution for a period of study but who are not admitted into a degree or diploma program. They are students at a foreign institution (often referred to as the student's home institution) who attend a Canadian institution (referred to as the student's host institution) for a period of time with the intent of transferring the credits earned at the host institution back to their home institution. Visiting students pay fees to the host institution.
Exchange students are students who have been admitted to an institution as visiting students. However, they are not subject to any tuition fees from their host institution, as these fees are covered by an exchange agreement between the host and home institutions. In most cases, exchange students do not require a study permit, since their length of stay is usually less than 6 months. However, they may still apply for a study permit. For programs of 6 months or longer in duration, exchange students must apply for a study permit. Students participating in exchange programs are eligible to work off campus only if they hold a study permit. The processing officer must include the appropriate work authorization conditions when issuing a study permit to exchange students.
Note: While a study permit is not required for short-term courses, an officer must accept
and process an application for a study permit, even when the duration of the course or program of study is 6 months or less [R188(2)].
Foreign nationals who are in Canada as visitors and are authorized to apply for a study permit from within Canada under section R215(1)(f) may begin their studies once they have submitted their study permit application, provided the application has been submitted before the expiry of their visitor status. They are required to cease studying if their study permit application is refused.
Prerequisite course or program of study in Canada before the main program of study As of June 1, 2014, visitors in Canada who have completed a course or program of study that was previously identified as a prerequisite for their admission into a program of study at a DLI may also apply for a study permit from within Canada [R215(1)(f)(iii)] if they provide both

- proof of successful completion of the prerequisite course, such as a letter from the destination DLI explicitly confirming that the student has completed the prerequisite course or program of study or a notification of completion from the institution at which the prerequisite course was taken

- unable to provide a letter of acceptance issued by a DLI either before or after the prerequisite course that proves the course is a prerequisite for entry to the main program
- admitted to a program with a language requirement, but a specific language training course or program is not specified in the letter of acceptance as a prerequisite for entry to the main program (for example, wording such as “must provide proof of English proficiency" does not indicate the need for a prerequisite)

threads.subject: Reason for Spouse not accompanying -- REP-2020-2370
threads.question:
Hello there,
If the only reason for not including the Spouse as Accompanying in the Express Entry profile is the Decrease in CRS score, is it a legitimate reason to mention that the Spouse is not accompanying due to low CRS and will come later through Spousal Sponsorship?
threads.answer:
Good Day,
Thank you for your email correspondence to 's Immigration Representatives mailbox. We appreciate your patience.
Question: If the only reason for not including the Spouse as Accompanying in the Express Entry profile is the Decrease in CRS score, is it a legitimate reason to mention that the Spouse is not accompanying due to low CRS and will come later through Spousal Sponsorship?
Answer: The differing points grid in Express Entry was developed to reflect the increased economic success in Canada seen where the principal applicant has a spouse possessing certain competencies. IRCC does not support the use of these provisions in any kind of “strategic” way. We recommend that spouses who intend to live together in Canada, state that in their applications, and work to increase their CRS score while waiting in the pool for an invitation. While changing the spouse's status from “accompanying” to "non-accompanying" during the processing of an application, up to the time of landing, may not constitute misrepresentation, this choice was never intended to be used as a strategy. Rather, it allows families to accurately describe their situation and intentions and to comply with section 16 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act on the obligation to answer truthfully. We trust that this information will assist you.
Sincerely,
Immigration Representatives Mailbox

threads.subject: Seeking Guidance on Extension Applications-Location of Applicant at time of application submission -- REP- 2020-2330
threads.question:
Hello,
Question: I am seeking your guidance as to whether there is any legal bar or possible repercussions for someone who holds a valid work or study permit, has a Canadian residential address and is ordinarily resident in Canada as a temporary resident, who submits an application to extend their work or study permit online while they are physically outside of Canada (presently with many employers having their entire teams work remotely for the foreseeable future, some foreign worker employees have temporarily returned to their home countries to work remotely so that they can also be with their families and this question has therefore arisen).
Response: Paragraph 183(4)(a) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations states:
(4) The period authorized for a temporary resident's stay ends on the earliest of
(a) the day on which the temporary resident leaves Canada without obtaining prior authorization to re-enter Canada;
Because the employees/students have left Canada, they no longer have temporary resident status and therefore do not have any status to extend. Holding a work or study permit does not grant a foreign national temporary resident status on its own; rather it only provides the foreign national with authorization to work or study in Canada. A foreign national is granted temporary resident status upon examination by an officer at a port of entry as per subsection 22(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act:
22 (1) A foreign national becomes a temporary resident if an officer is satisfied that the foreign national has applied for that status, has met the obligations set out in paragraph 20(1)(b), is not inadmissible and is not the subject of a declaration made under subsection 22.1(1).
Given the above, the foreign nationals in this situation would not be able to submit an application to extend their status if they are physically outside of Canada (please note that a work permit is not required if a foreign national working for a Canadian employer is not physically in Canada). For foreign nationals planning on returning to Canada to work or study: If their initial work/study permit is still valid and they have a valid TRV/eTA (if applicable): they may travel to Canada and will be assessed by an officer at the port of entry to determine whether they may re-enter as a temporary resident. If they are permitted re-entry, only then may they apply to extend their work or study permit using the Application to Change Conditions or Extend Your Stay in Canada [IMM 5710] (PDF, 0.58 MB) or the Application to Change Conditions, Extend my stay or Remain in Canada as a Student [IMM 5709] (PDF, 488.83 KB) If their initial work/study permit has expired: the foreign national must apply for a new work or study permit from outside of Canada.
Thank you,
The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

To assess an application under section A11.2, a processing office must consider the information in an applicant's profile at the time of the round of invitations and the information provided when the applicant submits their e-APR. After an e-APR is submitted, an application cannot be refused due to a change in circumstance unless
- the officer determines that the change occurred before the applicant submitted their e-APR and that the change would have caused the applicant to be refused under section A11.2: therefore, the application should be refused under section A11.2; or
- the change in circumstance means the applicant no longer meets the minimum requirements of the program to which they are applying; therefore, the application may still meet the requirements of section A11.2 but can be refused for failing to meet program requirements.
For example, if an applicant marries or enters a common-law relationship before they submit their e-APR but informs IRCC of the marriage or common-law relationship only after they submit their e-APR, the marriage or common-law relationship can be taken into account as part of the section A11.2 assessment.
If, however, an applicant marries or enters a common-law relationship after they submit their e-APR, then informs IRCC of the marriage or common-law relationship, the marriage or common-law relationship cannot be taken into account as part of the section A11.2 assessment. However, the change in circumstance may affect whether the applicant still meets the program requirements. A change in an applicant's family circumstances may affect the applicant's eligibility, depending on the settlement funds required by the program to which they are applying.

To assess an application under section A11.2, a processing office must consider the information in an applicant's profile at the time of the round of invitations and the information provided when the applicant submits their e-APR. After an e-APR is submitted, an application cannot be refused due to a change in circumstance unless
the officer determines that the change occurred before the applicant submitted their e-APR and that the change would have caused the applicant to be refused under section A11.2: therefore, the application should be refused under section A11.2; or
- the change in circumstance means the applicant no longer meets the minimum requirements of the program to which they are applying; therefore, the application may still meet the requirements of section A11.2 but can be refused for failing to meet program requirements.

nmigration, Réfugiés

If, however, an applicant marries after they submit their e-APR, then informs IRCC of the marriage, the marriage cannot be taken into account as part of the section A11.2 assessment. However, the change in circumstance may affect whether the applicant still meets the program requirements. threads.subject: Temporary Resident Status in Canada--REP-2020-1646
threads.question:
Dear Officer,
I have a question about Foreign Nationals' (FN) temporary status in Canada.
1. Can an FN hold two statuses simultaneously? For example, I know that an FN can have a study permit and a work permit at the same time. If he was asked of his status, can he say that he is both or he is one or the other? In other words, is a status and a permit are interchangeable in this case? Or the one obtained first becomes his status?
2. When a Work Permit (WP) holder applies for an extension before his WP expires is considered to be on implied status. Therefore he can continue to work for the same employer, under the same conditions, etc., until a decision is made. What if he also applies for a Visitor Record (VR), thinking to avoid being out of status in Canada, and his VR gets approved before his WP extension application. In this situation:
a. Does he lose his implied status?
b. Does he need to stop working?
c. What is his status?
Kind regards,
threads.answer:
Hello
Thank you for your inquiry. Kindly see the responses below.
1.Can an FN hold two statuses simultaneously? For example, I know that an FN can have a study permit and a work permit at the same time. If he was asked of his status, can he say that he is both or he is one or the other? In other words, is a status and a permit are interchangeable in this case? Or the one obtained first becomes his status? Response: A temporary resident is a foreign national who is legally authorized to enter Canada for temporary purposes. A foreign national has temporary resident status when they have been found to meet the requirements of the legislation to enter and/or remain in Ċanada as a visitor, student, worker or temporary resident permit holder. Only foreign nationals physically in Canada hold temporary resident status. The use of the words “status” and “permit” (authorization) are not interchangeable. A foreign national may hold more than one permit simultaneously. For example, a client may hold both a PGWP from a previously completed program and a study permit for another program of study simultaneously. Both permits indicate a temporary resident status in Canada.
2. When a Work Permit (WP) holder applies for an extension before his WP expires is considered to be on implied status. Therefore he can continue to work for the same employer, under the same conditions, etc., until a decision is made. What if he also applies for a Visitor Record (VR), thinking to avoid being out of status in Canada, and his VR gets approved before his WP extension application. In this situation:
a. Does he lose his implied status?
b. Does he need to stop working?
c. What is his status?
Response:
It should be noted that “status” and “authorization” are separate in the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA). A foreign national who submits the “Application to change conditions or extend my stay in Canada — Worker” application form [IMM 5710] is in effect submitting two applications in one. The foreign national is applying under section R181 for an “extension of status” and under section R201 of to “renew the work permit”.
The application for renewal under section R201 triggers the ability for the foreign national to “work without a permit” under paragraph R186(u). As per paragraph R186(u), the foreign national retains authorization to work without a work permit untiī a decision is rendered on the application made under R201 (or this authorization ends if they leave Canada before a decision is rendered). The issuance of a Visitor Record does not end this authorization, although it does ensure that the foreign national retains their temporary resident status in the event that their work permit extension application is refused.

threads.subject: questions -- REP-2020-2402
threads.question:
## Bonjour à vous
Je vous écris concernant la politique d’intérêt public visant les dispenses des conditions du permis de travail dans le cas d’un changement d’emploi ( execution des programmes sur la Covid), il y a beaucoup de confusion parmi mes collègues sur la politique.
Je voudrais m’assurer d’avoir la bonne réponse à conseiller aux clients.
Mes questions sont :
Un travailleur a déposé une demande de changement de conditions de son permis de travail .Son employeur a déja fait une demande EIMT/ CAQ mais n’a pas encore reçu la décision. Lors du dépôt de la demande du permis de travailleur, celui-ci a fourni les preuves que le EIMT /CAQ ont été déposées mais que la décision n’a pas encore été rendue :
1) Est ce que le travailleur peut quand meme bénéficier de cette politique ?
2) Est ce que le travailleur n ayant pas encore eu la réponse favorable du EIMT /CAQ peut déposer sa demande de changement de condition du permis de travail en tout temps ou bien doit il attendre absolument 14 jours avant l’échéance de son permis de travail pour le faire ?
3) J ai un travailleur dont le permis de travail vient à échéance en Février. Nous sommes à faire une nouvelle demande d’EIMT et CAQ pour une nouvelle profession ( son CNP changera) qui sera soumise vers le 15 décembre. Ensuite, vers le 18 décembre, nous voudrions immédiatement procéder à la demande de changement des conditions de son permis de travail en fournissant bien sur les preuves de dépot des demandes EIMT et CAQ. Est ce que le travailleur peut bénéficier de la procédure d’intérêt public de changement
d’emploi immédiatement meme si son permis vient à échéance en février ?
Je vous remercie beaucoup et portez vous bien.
threads.answer:
Bonjour
Questions: Un travailleur a déposé une demande de changement de conditions de son permis de travail .Son employeura déja fait une demande EIMT/ CAQ mais n’a pas encore reçu la décision. Lors du dépôt de la demande du permis de travailleur, celui-ci a fourni les preuves que le EIMT /CAQ ont été déposées mais que la décision n’a pas encore été rendue :
1) Est ce que le travailleur peut quand meme bénéficier de cette politique ?
2) Est ce que le travailleur n ‘ayant pas encore eu la réponse favorable du EIMT /CAQ peut déposer sa demande de changement de condition du permis de travail en tout temps ou bien doit il attendre absolument 14jours avant l’échéance de son permis de travail pour le faire?
3) J ai un travailleur dont le permis de travail vient à échéance en Février. Nous sommes à faire une nouvelle demande d’EIMT et CAQ pour une nouvelle profession (son CNP changera) qui sera soumise vers le 15 décembre. Ensuite, vers le 18 décembre, nous voudrions immédiatement procéder à la demande de changement des conditions de son permis de travail en fournissant bien sur les preuves de dépot des demandes EIMT et CAQ. Est ce que le travailleur peut bénéficier de la procédure d’intérêt public de changement d’emploi immédiatement meme si son permis vient à échéance en février ?
Réponses :
1) Oui le travailleur peut quand même bénéficier de la politique d’intérêt public, en autant qu’il soumette une preuve comme quoi l’employeur a fait une demande d’EIMT.
2) Il peut le faire en tout temps.
3) Oui, comme les conditions d’emploi changeront, il n’a pas à attendre pour faire la demande et peut bénéficier de la politique d’intérêt public avec la preuve que l’EIMT a été déposée.
Nous vous remercions d’avoir communiqué avec la Division de la prestation des programmes des résidents temporaires d’IRCC. Nous ne pouvons répondre aux demandes de renseignements portant sur des cas précis, mais nous vous encourageons à communiquer avec la ressource compétente indiquée ci--dessous pour obtenir de l’aide.
1) Pour obtenir de plus amples renseignements au sujet des programmes d'IRCC, veuillez consulter le Centre d’aide
2) Pour savoir où en est rendu le traitement de votre demande, vous pouvez vérifierl'état de votre demande en ligne.
3) Pour toute autre question, veuillez communiquer avecle Ministère selon le moyen approprié indiqué surla page Contactez--nous.
4) Si vous avez déjà communiqué avecle Centre de soutien à la clientèle ou le bureau migration au sujet du traitement de votre demande et/ou des motifs de la décision, et avez besoin de renseignements supplémentaires, vous pouvez communiquer avec l’Unité des cas et conseils au Règlement des cas par courriel.
5) Si vous éprouvez des problèmes techniques avecle Portail de l'employeur, veuillez envoyer votre question à la boîte aux lettres du Portail de l’employeur. Les employeurs devraient s’assurer de réviser le Guide d’'inscription ainsi que le Guide d’utilisation du Portail des employeurs.
6) Les employeurs qui souhaitent embaucher un travailleur qui se trouve à l’extérieur du Canada et qui vient d’un pays dispensé de l’obligation de visa et qui est possiblement dispensé d’une étude d’impact sur le marché du travail (ElMT) ou d'un permis de travail, peuvent envoyer un courriel à l'Unité pour la mobilité internationale des travailleurs afin d'obtenir un avis. Il n'y a pas de frais associés pour les demandes d’avis. Les avis fournis par I'Unité pour la mobilité internationale des travailleurs peuvent être pris en compte par l’agent des services frontaliers mais ne garantissent pas que le travailleur sera dispensé d’une ElMT ou d’un permis de travail ou qu’il sera admis au Canada.

threads.subject: Foreign Work Experience and Self-Employment in Express Entry -- REP-2020-2409
threads.question:
Hello,
I have a question with respect to self-employment and foreign work experience under the Ministerial Instructions for Express Entry and the awarding of points under skills transferability factors.
MI Article 25 states:
25 (1) For the purposes of sections 23 and 24, foreign work experience is work experience that
(a) is acquired by a foreign national outside Canada in one or more occupations listed in Skill Type 0 Management Occupations or Skill Level A or B of the National Occupational Classification matrix;
(b) consists of full-time work experience, or the full-time equivalent for part-time work experience, with one or more employers;
(c) is acquired within the 10-year period preceding the day on which points are assigned to the foreign national under section 23 or subsection 24(1); and
(d) is remunerated by the payment of wages or a commission
The section does not explicitly exclude self-employment, whichis the case for Canadian work experience in accordance with MI 15(7):
(7) For the purposes of this section,
and Citizenshi Canada et Ciloyeneé Canada
(a) a period of employment during which the foreign national was engaged in full-time study is not to be included in calculating a period of work experience;
(b) a period of self-employment or unauthorized work is not to be included in calculating a period of work experience;
(c) the foreign national must have had temporary resident status during their period of work experience and any period of full-time study or training; and
(d) the full-time equivalent for part-time work experience is 30 hours of work per week.
If foreign work experience were obtained by means of self-employment that is paid by wages (a scenario that is potentially possible if, for example, someone were to create a business and employ themselves with a salary), would it count?
Sincerely,
and Cizenship Canadaot Cioyenneté Canada
